examples.en: Our worksheet places a communications outtake after message delivery and before longer changes in the fictional timeline.
examples.zh: 练习单在虚构时间线中，把「受众即时反应」放在消息传达之后、较长期的变化之前。

collocations: audience understanding as a communications outtake

words.enDefinition: A working document that sets out communication activities, responsibilities, timing, and evaluation for specified objectives.

examples.en: The fictional university's communications plan lists who will publish each notice about the replacement study space.
examples.zh: 虚构大学的「传播计划」列明关于替代自习空间的各项通知将由谁发布。

examples.en: Our class checks whether the communications plan includes a timetable for answering public questions about the change.
examples.zh: 全班核对「传播计划」是否包含回答公众对该变化所提问题的时间表。

words.enDefinition: An overall approach specifying how communication is intended to support organisational goals and audience needs.

examples.en: The fictional recreation centre's communications strategy explains how residents will learn about new booking arrangements.
examples.zh: 虚构活动中心的「传播策略」解释了居民将如何获知新的预约安排。

examples.en: Our class assesses whether the communications strategy addresses the concerns listed in the sample public feedback report.
examples.zh: 全班评估「传播策略」是否回应了公众反馈报告样本中列出的关切。

words.enDefinition: A session giving members of a community information and context about a local issue, activity, or decision.

examples.en: At the community briefing, a representative explained how the fictional garden would reopen after the pathways were repaired.
examples.zh: 在「社区情况说明会」上，一名代表解释了虚构花园将在路径维修后怎样重新开放。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks which community briefing in the fictional schedule is intended for neighbouring residents this week.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，虚构日程里哪场「社区情况说明会」本周面向附近居民。

words.enDefinition: A person designated to maintain communication between an organisation and local residents or groups.

examples.en: The fictional museum names a community liaison officer for residents with questions about the building work nearby.
examples.zh: 虚构博物馆指定一名「社区联络专员」，供对附近施工有疑问的居民联系。

examples.en: Our exercise asks how the community liaison officer reports recurring questions to the staff responsible for the project.
examples.zh: 练习询问，「社区联络专员」怎样向项目负责人反映反复出现的问题。

collocations: responsibilities of a community liaison officer

words.enDefinition: An organisation's work to develop and maintain constructive relationships with the communities affected by its activities.

examples.en: The sample report describes community relations through a fictional museum's ongoing dialogue with residents around the site.
examples.zh: 样本报告通过虚构博物馆与周边居民的持续对话，描述「社区关系」工作。

examples.en: Our class discusses community relations using examples of joint events between a fictional college and nearby groups.
examples.zh: 课堂用虚构大学与附近团体合办活动的例子讨论「社区关系」。

words.enDefinition: A communication informing a local or affected community about recent changes, progress, or decisions.

examples.en: The fictional museum issues a community update about the revised schedule for its weekend reading programme.
examples.zh: 虚构博物馆发布一份「面向社区的最新通报」，介绍周末阅读项目调整后的时段。

examples.en: Our class examines whether the community update addresses questions raised by residents in the fictional listening session.
examples.zh: 全班看「面向社区的最新通报」是否回应了居民在虚构意见听取会上提出的问题。

words.enDefinition: a banner displayed alongside a video or audio advertisement as a related creative element

examples.en: A companion banner beside the video repeated the exhibition dates shown in the spoken message.
examples.zh: 视频旁的「伴随横幅广告」重复了口播里的展览日期。

examples.en: The designer made the companion banner use the same colors as the short audio spot.
examples.zh: 设计师让「伴随横幅广告」沿用短音频广告的配色。

words.enDefinition: advertising that explicitly or implicitly compares an offering with a competing offering

examples.en: The tutor checked whether the comparative advertising used the same test conditions for both kettles.
examples.zh: 导师查看「比较广告」是否在相同条件下测试两款水壶。

examples.en: The company based its comparative advertising on published figures for two standard service plans.
examples.zh: 公司将两种标准服务方案的公开数据用在了「比较广告」里。

words.enDefinition: A way of evaluating options that allows strengths on one attribute to compensate for weaknesses on another.

examples.en: The fictional comparison illustrates a compensatory decision rule when lower weight offsets reduced storage space for one buyer.
examples.zh: 虚构比较中，对于一位买家而言，重量更轻弥补了收纳空间变小，体现「补偿性决策规则」。

examples.en: Our textbook uses a compensatory decision rule to explain how two attributes can contribute to the overall judgement.
examples.zh: 教材用「补偿性决策规则」说明两项属性如何共同影响总体判断。

words.enDefinition: Setting prices mainly with reference to competing offers in the market

examples.en: The case illustrates competition-based pricing by starting from the prices of rival products.
examples.zh: 案例从竞争产品的价格出发，说明「竞争导向定价」。

examples.en: We contrasted competition-based pricing with pricing based only on the seller's costs.
examples.zh: 我们将「竞争导向定价」与仅根据卖家成本定价作了比较。

collocations: compare competition-based pricing with cost estimates

words.enDefinition: The category or alternatives against which customers are meant to evaluate the brand.

examples.en: Our competitive frame of reference included ordinary desk organizers because students compared the new item with them.
examples.zh: 学生用普通桌面收纳架与新品比较，所以我们的「竞争参照框架」涵盖了这类收纳架。

examples.en: The instructor asked whether the competitive frame of reference should include both shared storage and portable cases.
examples.zh: 老师问，「竞争参照框架」是否应同时包含共享收纳设施和便携收纳盒。

collocations: define the competitive frame of reference
select a competitive frame of reference
change the competitive frame of reference

words.enDefinition: a budgeting method that uses competitors' advertising expenditure as the main reference for setting one's own budget

examples.en: The regional chain used the competitive-parity method to compare its proposal with competitors' estimated spending.
examples.zh: 这家地区连锁用「竞争对等预算法」，把自身提案与竞争对手的估计广告开支相比较。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether the competitive-parity method was useful when similar firms released no spending figures.
examples.zh: 导师问，同类企业没有公布支出数据时，「竞争对等预算法」是否有用。

words.enDefinition: An attribute or benefit matching a competitor closely enough to neutralize its advantage.

examples.en: The fictional shop added a similar repair service to establish a competitive point of parity with its rival.
examples.zh: 虚构商店增设了相似的维修服务，与对手形成一项「竞争对等点」。

examples.en: We identified a competitive point of parity when both fictional brands offered the same useful replacement feature.
examples.zh: 两个虚构品牌都提供同一种实用的替换功能时，我们找出了一项「竞争对等点」。

collocations: establish a competitive point of parity
a competitive point of parity on reliability
identify a competitive point of parity

words.enDefinition: The specific set of competitors used for a market or positioning comparison.

examples.en: We built a competitive set from the three desk accessory brands mentioned most often by fictional buyers.
examples.zh: 我们取虚构买家最常提到的三个桌面用品品牌，组成「竞争品牌参照组」。

examples.en: The competitive set changed after our case moved from campus bookstores to shops with broader assortments.
examples.zh: 案例所考察的店从校园书店换成品类更多的商店后，「竞争品牌参照组」也变了。

collocations: compare brands in a competitive set

words.enDefinition: In a consumer behaviour framework, a pattern of high involvement and perceived differences between alternatives.

examples.en: The worksheet describes complex buying behavior when a fictional shopper compares meaningfully different options for a long-term purchase.
examples.zh: 练习单以虚构购物者为一项长期购买对比存在实质差异的选项为例，说明「复杂购买行为」。

examples.en: Our seminar identifies complex buying behavior by checking both purchase importance and the perceived differences in the example.
examples.zh: 研讨课核看示例的购买重要性和感知差异，以辨认「复杂购买行为」。

words.enDefinition: How attractive or interesting potential consumers find a proposed product idea under the stated evaluation conditions.

examples.en: The fictional results compare concept appeal for two proposed containers using the same question and response scale.
examples.zh: 虚构结果采用同一问题和回答量表，比较两款拟议容器的「产品概念吸引力」。

examples.en: Our class discusses concept appeal separately from the feasibility of making the fictional item on campus.
examples.zh: 全班将「产品概念吸引力」与在校园制作该虚构物品的可行性分开讨论。

words.enDefinition: Assessing reactions to a proposed offering before developing or launching the final product.

examples.en: The class used concept testing to compare two proposed bag designs before either existed as a sample.
examples.zh: 课堂用「产品概念测试」比较两款包袋方案，当时两款都还没有样品。

examples.en: Concept testing in the fictional project asked students which benefit they understood from a short description.
examples.zh: 虚构项目的「产品概念测试」询问学生，读过简短描述后理解了产品的哪项好处。

words.enDefinition: Viewers watching the measured stream at the same point in time

examples.en: The live report plots concurrent viewers as the fictional event progresses through its schedule.
examples.zh: 直播报告按虚构活动的进行时序绘制「同时在线观众」人数。

examples.en: We distinguished concurrent viewers from everyone who watched at any point during the evening.
examples.zh: 我们将「同时在线观众」与当晚任意时刻看过节目的人区分开来。

words.enDefinition: Details that have been checked and established as reliable for the purposes of a communication.

examples.en: The fictional museum's update separates confirmed information about opening hours from details still awaiting confirmation that morning.
examples.zh: 虚构博物馆上午发布的通报把关于开放时间的「已确认的信息」与尚待确认的细节分开。

examples.en: Our exercise asks which parts of the public statement are confirmed information according to the fictional records.
examples.zh: 练习询问，根据虚构记录，公开声明的哪些部分属于「已确认的信息」。

words.zhGloss: 各项均须达标的决策规则
words.enDefinition: A rule accepting an option only if it meets minimum standards on every selected attribute.
acceptedZhAnswers: 各项均须达标的决策规则

examples.en: The fictional shopper follows a conjunctive decision rule by keeping only boxes that meet both size requirements.
examples.zh: 虚构购物者采用「各项均须达标的决策规则」，只保留符合两个尺寸要求的盒子。

examples.en: Our worksheet uses a conjunctive decision rule to explain why one missed requirement eliminates an otherwise acceptable choice.
examples.zh: 练习单用「各项均须达标的决策规则」说明，为什么缺一项要求就会排除原本可以接受的选项。

collocations: minimum standards in a conjunctive decision rule

words.enDefinition: The subset of available options a consumer actively considers for a particular choice.

examples.en: The fictional shopper narrows the consideration set to two pencil cases before examining how each one closes.
examples.zh: 虚构购物者把「认真考虑的备选集合」缩小到两个笔袋，然后查看各自的闭合方式。

examples.en: Our class compares the consideration set with the longer list of items available in the sample catalogue.
examples.zh: 全班把「认真考虑的备选集合」与样本目录中较长的可选物品列表作比较。

words.enDefinition: Audience estimates combining live viewing and eligible playback within a stated reporting window

examples.en: The Barb worksheet gives consolidated viewing for a stated period after the original transmission.
examples.zh: Barb 习题给出了首次播出后指定时段内的「合并收视数据」。

examples.en: We compared consolidated viewing with figures published the morning after the programme aired.
examples.zh: 我们把「合并收视数据」与节目播出次日上午发布的数值作了比较。

collocations: compare consolidated viewing with overnight figures

words.enDefinition: A concise account of the main views and themes raised during a consultation.

examples.en: The fictional consultation summary records several views about extending opening hours and explains how responses were grouped.
examples.zh: 虚构「意见征询摘要」记录了几种关于延长开放时间的意见，并解释答复如何分类。

examples.en: Our worksheet identifies which concerns in the consultation summary are mentioned again in the fictional decision document.
examples.zh: 练习单辨认「意见征询摘要」中哪些关切再次出现在虚构决定文件中。

words.enDefinition: How individuals or households choose, acquire, and respond to products or services for personal use.

examples.en: The module introduces consumer buying behavior through fictional accounts of students choosing supplies for shared studio work.
examples.zh: 课程单元通过虚构学生选择共用工作室用品的记述，介绍「消费者购买行为」。

examples.en: Our seminar compares consumer buying behavior for ordinary supplies with decisions about longer-lasting items in the same category.
examples.zh: 研讨课比较购买普通用品和同类耐用品时的「消费者购买行为」。

words.enDefinition: A framework describing stages such as recognising a need, exploring options, choosing, and evaluating the outcome.

examples.en: The diagram illustrates the consumer decision process through a fictional purchase of a reusable lunch container.
examples.zh: 示意图用虚构的可重复使用餐盒购买案例说明「消费者决策过程」。

examples.en: Our textbook notes that the consumer decision process may include fewer steps for familiar routine purchases.
examples.zh: 教材指出，购买熟悉的日常用品时，「消费者决策过程」可能包含较少步骤。

collocations: stages of the consumer decision process
model of the consumer decision process

words.enDefinition: A negative evaluation of how a product or service performed in use or purchase.

examples.en: The fictional survey summary records consumer dissatisfaction with a folder described as difficult to close in class.
examples.zh: 虚构调查摘要记录了因文件夹据说在课堂上不好合上而产生的「消费者不满」。

examples.en: Our discussion compares consumer dissatisfaction with reports of product performance in the same fictional student sample.
examples.zh: 课堂讨论把「消费者不满」与相同虚构学生样本所报告的产品表现作比较。

words.enDefinition: The attributes or standards a consumer uses to compare possible purchases.

examples.en: The fictional shopper lists durability and space as consumer evaluative criteria for choosing a studio storage box.
examples.zh: 虚构购物者选工作室储物盒时，将耐用性和空间列为「消费者的评估标准」。

examples.en: Our seminar compares consumer evaluative criteria across two fictional buyers with different uses for the same item.
examples.zh: 研讨课对比两名对同一物品用途不同的虚构买家的「消费者的评估标准」。

words.enDefinition: An evidence-informed understanding of a consumer need, motive, or pattern that helps explain observed choices or attitudes.

examples.en: The class develops a consumer insight by comparing why fictional shoppers chose similar items for different reasons.
examples.zh: 全班比较虚构购物者为何出于不同原因挑选相似物品，据此形成一项「消费者洞察」。

examples.en: Our worksheet distinguishes a consumer insight from a single raw percentage in the sample study's summary table.
examples.zh: 练习单把「消费者洞察」与研究样本汇总表里的单一原始百分比分开。

words.enDefinition: How personally relevant or important a product or buying decision feels to a consumer in context.

examples.en: The tutor introduces consumer involvement through two fictional shoppers who assign very different importance to the purchase.
examples.zh: 老师借两名对这次购买重视程度迥异的虚构购物者介绍「消费者涉入度」。

examples.en: Our worksheet describes consumer involvement separately from how many alternatives are actually available in the sample catalogue.
examples.zh: 练习单对「消费者涉入度」单独作了描述，与样本目录中实际有多少选项分开。

words.enDefinition: An internal reason or drive behind a consumer's pursuit of a purchasing or consumption goal.

examples.en: The casebook compares consumer motivation across fictional students choosing the same kitchen item for different reasons.
examples.zh: 案例教材比较几名因不同原因挑选同一厨具的虚构学生的「消费者动机」。

examples.en: Our seminar discusses consumer motivation after reading several accounts of why the fictional shoppers began searching.
examples.zh: 研讨课阅读了几段讲述虚构购物者为什么开始搜寻的记述，然后讨论「消费者动机」。

words.enDefinition: A concise description of the outcome or practical problem a consumer needs addressed, usually independent of any proposed solution.

examples.en: The fictional brief includes a consumer need statement about keeping large papers flat during travel to class.
examples.zh: 虚构简报给出一条「消费者需求陈述」，内容是在去上课的路上使大幅纸张保持平整。

examples.en: Our class compares the consumer need statement with a later proposal naming one specific design for a folder.
examples.zh: 全班把「消费者需求陈述」与后来指出文件夹某种具体设计的提案作比较。

collocations: support a consumer need statement with evidence

words.enDefinition: A group of people who have agreed to be invited to take part in consumer research studies over time.

examples.en: The fictional research provider describes a consumer research panel whose members can choose whether to answer each survey.
examples.zh: 虚构调研机构介绍了一个「消费者调研样本库」，成员可选择是否参加每次调查。

examples.en: Our worksheet distinguishes a consumer research panel from the subset of fictional members who joined one particular study.
examples.zh: 练习单区分「消费者调研样本库」和参加某次具体研究的虚构成员子集。

collocations: sample from a consumer research panel
voluntary participation in a consumer research panel

words.enDefinition: The process of learning skills, norms, and habits involved in participating in consumer life.

examples.en: The casebook illustrates consumer socialization through a fictional student learning how a household compares everyday products.
examples.zh: 案例教材用虚构学生学习一个家庭如何比较日常商品的例子，说明「消费者社会化」。

examples.en: Our lecture considers how different social settings can contribute to consumer socialization in the classroom examples.
examples.zh: 讲座讨论，在课堂示例中，不同的社会环境如何参与「消费者社会化」。

words.enDefinition: A direct quotation from a consumer's response used to illustrate a point in a research report or presentation.

examples.en: The fictional report labels a consumer verbatim beside the aggregate finding it is intended to illustrate in class.
examples.zh: 虚构报告把一则「消费者原话摘录」标在它准备于课堂说明的汇总发现旁。

examples.en: Our tutor asks whether the consumer verbatim illustrates the finding or represents the entire group of fictional respondents.
examples.zh: 老师询问，「消费者原话摘录」是用于说明这一发现，还是能代表全部虚构应答者。

words.enDefinition: An outcome a consumer hopes to achieve through choosing or using a product or service.

examples.en: In the fictional vignette, the consumption goal is keeping drawing supplies organised during a shared studio session.
examples.zh: 在虚构材料中，「消费目标」是在共有工作室活动中将绘画用品摆放整齐。

examples.en: Our worksheet identifies the consumption goal before assessing which characteristics of the products would support it.
examples.zh: 练习单先找出「消费目标」，再评估产品的哪些特点有助于实现它。

collocations: product associated with a consumption goal

words.enDefinition: Information stating when, where, and how a title may be offered

examples.en: The platform checks content avails before adding a title to its regional catalogue.
examples.zh: 平台在把一部作品加入地区片库之前查看「内容发行可用信息」。

examples.en: We compared the content avails for two territories with different release windows.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两个发行窗口不同地区的「内容发行可用信息」。

words.enDefinition: advertising selected according to the topic or content of the page or programme where it appears

examples.en: The guide uses contextual advertising when a hiking equipment ad appears beside an article about trails.
examples.zh: 徒步装备广告出现在步道文章旁，指南用它来说明「语境广告」。

examples.en: The class examined contextual advertising on a cooking page featuring an advertisement for kitchen scales.
examples.zh: 课堂用烹饪网页上的厨房秤广告来分析「语境广告」。

words.enDefinition: On-set notes tracking details that should match across takes and setups

examples.en: The continuity notes record which hand the actor used to open the notebook.
examples.zh: 「连贯性记录」注明演员用哪只手打开笔记本。

examples.en: We consulted the continuity notes before shooting the same exchange from another angle.
examples.zh: 我们先查阅「连贯性记录」，再从另一角度拍同一段对话。

words.enDefinition: a scheduling pattern that keeps advertising active without planned gaps during the campaign period

examples.en: The agency chose continuous scheduling so the programme announcement would appear throughout the semester.
examples.zh: 机构选择「连续式广告排期」，让项目公告在整个学期持续出现。

examples.en: Our class compared continuous scheduling with a plan containing several weeks without any placements.
examples.zh: 课堂比较了「连续式广告排期」与一份相隔几周没有投放的方案。

words.enDefinition: Coordinated distribution system in which independent firms cooperate under formal agreements

examples.en: The textbook uses an invented franchise network to illustrate a contractual vertical marketing system.
examples.zh: 教材用虚构的特许经营网络举例说明「契约型垂直营销系统」。

examples.en: We discussed how independent parties could coordinate under a contractual vertical marketing system in the case.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了案例中的独立各方如何在「契约型垂直营销系统」中协调运作。

collocations: form a contractual vertical marketing system
participants in a contractual vertical marketing system
model a contractual vertical marketing system

words.enDefinition: an existing or standard advertisement version used as the comparison in a creative test

examples.en: The team used its familiar poster as the control creative when comparing two newly drafted versions.
examples.zh: 团队比较两份新稿时，用那张已为人熟悉的海报作「对照广告素材」。

examples.en: We kept the control creative unchanged throughout the class's two-week demonstration of advertising tests.
examples.zh: 课堂做了两周广告测试演示，我们始终让「对照广告素材」保持不变。

words.enDefinition: An offering typically bought frequently with little effort or comparison.

examples.en: In our retail exercise, the shop sold individual pens near the checkout as a convenience product.
examples.zh: 零售练习中，商店在结账区附近把单支笔作为「便利品」销售。

examples.en: Students identified a convenience product when the fictional buyers spent little time comparing their familiar options.
examples.zh: 虚构买家几乎不花时间比较熟悉的选项，学生由此辨认出一种「便利品」。

collocations: classify an item as a convenience product

words.enDefinition: Distribution system of independent firms pursuing their own objectives at each level

examples.en: The chart shows a conventional marketing system in which firms keep separate pricing decisions.
examples.zh: 图表展示了一个各家公司分别定价的「传统营销渠道系统」。

examples.en: We compared the conventional marketing system with a network coordinated under common ownership.
examples.zh: 我们将「传统营销渠道系统」与统一所有权下协调运作的网络作了比较。

collocations: members of a conventional marketing system

words.enDefinition: the increase in desired actions attributable to advertising, estimated through comparison with an appropriate baseline or control

examples.en: The study measured conversion lift in class registrations by comparing the campaign group with a holdout.
examples.zh: 研究比较宣传组和保留对照组，测量课程报名的「转化提升」。

examples.en: The campaign report listed many signups, but the experiment estimated only a small conversion lift.
examples.zh: 活动报告记录了许多报名，但实验估计的「转化提升」很小。

words.enDefinition: The latest time written material must be submitted for editorial processing.

examples.en: The copy deadline gave student editors an hour to check the facts before the newsletter went out.
examples.zh: 按「文稿截稿时间」收稿后，学生编辑在发简报前还有一小时可核对事实。

examples.en: We asked for an earlier copy deadline because the mock edition included several stories needing extra review.
examples.zh: 模拟刊物有好几篇稿件需要加审，我们因此要求提前「文稿截稿时间」。

words.enDefinition: The newsroom unit responsible for checking and preparing written material for publication.

examples.en: The copy desk queried the spelling of a building name before the campus article went online.
examples.zh: 校园报道上线前，「文字编辑台」请记者核实一栋楼的名称拼写。

examples.en: The student paper sent the completed story to the copy desk for a final review.
examples.zh: 学生报把完成的报道送交「文字编辑台」进行最后一次审读。

collocations: send an article to the copy desk
a query from the copy desk

words.enDefinition: To check and revise text for clarity, accuracy, consistency, grammar, or house style.

examples.en: The volunteer agreed to copy edit the campus story after the reporter verified the event details.
examples.zh: 志愿者同意等记者核实活动细节后，「校订」这篇校园报道。

examples.en: We learned to copy edit the newsletter without changing what the quoted students had originally said.
examples.zh: 我们练习如何「校订」这份简报，同时保留受访学生原来的表述。

collocations: copy edit a draft before publication

words.enDefinition: An editor who checks written copy for accuracy, clarity, consistency, and style.

examples.en: The copy editor checked the spelling of building names and the figures in the campus article.
examples.zh: 「文字编辑」核对了校园报道里的建筑名称拼写和数字。

examples.en: Our copy editor flagged a sentence whose pronoun could refer to either person in the interview.
examples.zh: 我们的「文字编辑」标出了一句有歧义的话，其中的代词可能指两位受访者中的任何一位。

collocations: send a draft to a copy editor

words.enDefinition: an outline of the central proposition, supporting arguments, and tone that will guide advertising copy

examples.en: The agency established a copy platform before assigning the brochure and email drafts to different writers.
examples.zh: 机构先拟定「文案策略纲要」，再把宣传册和邮件交给不同人写。

examples.en: The copy platform listed two reasons customers might prefer the service and a tone to maintain.
examples.zh: 「文案策略纲要」列出顾客偏好这项服务的两个理由，以及文案应保持的语气。

words.enDefinition: evaluation of an advertisement's wording or other creative elements with a sample audience

examples.en: The agency used copy testing to check whether viewers understood the advertisement's main promise.
examples.zh: 机构用「广告内容测试」了解观众是否读懂广告的主要承诺。

examples.en: Our class compared copy testing results for two brochures with different openings and layouts.
examples.zh: 课堂比较两份开头和排版各异的宣传册的「广告内容测试」结果。

words.enDefinition: The basic need an offering satisfies or the main outcome buyers seek.

examples.en: The team identified taking readable notes as the core benefit behind its classroom tablet concept.
examples.zh: 小组把记下清楚易读的笔记视为课堂平板概念要提供的「核心利益」。

examples.en: Our case compared two lamps with different designs but the same core benefit for students.
examples.zh: 案例比较了两款设计不同、却给学生带来相同「核心利益」的台灯。

collocations: the core benefit of the product

words.enDefinition: A brand representing the organization as a whole across offerings and audiences.

examples.en: The fictional stationery company's corporate brand appeared on its hiring pages and public reports as well as packaging.
examples.zh: 虚构文具公司的「企业品牌」既出现在包装上，也出现在招聘页面和公开报告中。

examples.en: We distinguished the corporate brand from the separate name on one line of notebooks in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们区分了「企业品牌」和单独印在一个笔记本系列上的名称。

collocations: the reputation of a corporate brand

words.enDefinition: An organisational function that coordinates communication with internal and external groups on behalf of a company.

examples.en: The sample organisation chart places corporate communications alongside several teams in a fictitious book distribution company.
examples.zh: 样本组织结构图把「企业传播」与一家虚构图书批发企业中的其他团队并列展示。

examples.en: Our seminar discusses corporate communications when comparing the company's staff bulletin with its public service announcement.
examples.zh: 研讨课对照公司内部员工简报和公开服务公告，讨论「企业传播」。

words.enDefinition: Coordinated distribution system with successive channel stages under common ownership

examples.en: The case shows a corporate vertical marketing system owned by the fictional notebook manufacturer.
examples.zh: 案例展示了一个由虚构笔记本制造商拥有的「公司型垂直营销系统」。

examples.en: We traced store ownership to identify the corporate vertical marketing system in the example.
examples.zh: 我们追踪了门店的所有权，以辨认出示例中的「公司型垂直营销系统」。

collocations: operate a corporate vertical marketing system
examples of a corporate vertical marketing system
ownership in a corporate vertical marketing system

words.enDefinition: A revised version of a previously issued release that fixes an error in its content.

examples.en: The fictional press office labels the corrected press release so readers can identify the version with accurate dates.
examples.zh: 虚构新闻联络办公室标注「更正后的公关新闻稿」，让读者能找到日期准确的版本。

examples.en: Our worksheet compares the corrected press release with the archived original to identify which information was changed.
examples.zh: 练习单比较「更正后的公关新闻稿」和存档原稿，找出哪些信息发生变动。

collocations: date of a corrected press release

words.enDefinition: A record identifying errors that were corrected and showing what was changed and when.

examples.en: The museum's correction log lists the date when staff fixed an incorrect opening time in a public notice.
examples.zh: 博物馆的「公开信息更正记录」列出了工作人员修正公告中错误开放时间的日期。

examples.en: Our class consults the correction log to see when the notice began showing the revised closing date.
examples.zh: 全班查阅「公开信息更正记录」，查看通知从什么时候开始显示调整后的结束日期。

collocations: add an entry to a correction log
date recorded in a correction log

words.enDefinition: A public notice in which an organization identifies an error in its own earlier communication and supplies the correct information.

examples.en: The fictional university posts a correction notice after its earlier announcement listed the wrong exhibition closing date.
examples.zh: 先前公告写错展览结束日期后，虚构大学发布了「更正通知」。

examples.en: Our class checks whether the correction notice identifies both the original error and the correct replacement date.
examples.zh: 全班核对「更正通知」是否同时指明原错误和替换后的正确日期。

words.enDefinition: Setting prices mainly from the cost of producing or delivering an offering

examples.en: The team modeled cost-based pricing before comparing prices with competing products in the exercise.
examples.zh: 团队先模拟「成本导向定价」，再在练习中与竞争产品的价格作比较。

examples.en: We discussed which cost categories were included in the cost-based pricing calculation.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「成本导向定价」的计算涵盖哪些成本类别。

words.enDefinition: the average advertising cost for acquiring one customer or completing another specified acquisition event

examples.en: The report gave cost per acquisition as total advertising spend divided by confirmed new subscribers.
examples.zh: 报告把广告总支出除以已确认的新订阅人数，得到「单次获客成本」。

examples.en: Our worksheet compares cost per acquisition after both campaigns use the same definition of a subscriber.
examples.zh: 练习单先让两项宣传使用同一个订阅者定义，再比较二者的「单次获客成本」。

words.enDefinition: the amount paid for each click, or average total cost divided by the number of clicks

examples.en: The student compared cost per click across two versions of the same exhibition advertisement.
examples.zh: 学生比较同一展览广告两个版本的「单次点击成本」。

examples.en: Cost per click rose when the campaign received fewer clicks at the same total cost.
examples.zh: 宣传活动总成本相同时，点击量下降使「单次点击成本」升高。

words.enDefinition: the average advertising cost for each viewing counted as a completed video view

examples.en: The team calculated cost per completed view after separating full video views from partial views.
examples.zh: 团队把完整观看和部分观看分开后，计算了「单次完整观看成本」。

examples.en: The worksheet asks which campaign had the lower cost per completed view at the same budget.
examples.zh: 练习问，同等预算下哪个宣传活动的「单次完整观看成本」更低。

words.enDefinition: the cost of delivering one thousand advertising impressions

examples.en: The planner compared cost per mille for two digital magazines with the same placement dimensions.
examples.zh: 规划人员比较了两份电子杂志同尺寸广告位的「千次展示成本」。

examples.en: Our class calculated cost per mille using the total price and the number of impressions delivered.
examples.zh: 课堂根据总价和实际交付的展示量计算「千次展示成本」。

collocations: compare cost per mille across channels

words.enDefinition: An examination of coverage to understand what was reported, how it was presented, and which themes were prominent.

examples.en: The fictional coverage analysis compares how different local outlets described the university's changes to its reading services.
examples.zh: 虚构「媒体报道分析」比较不同地方媒体如何描述大学对阅读服务的调整。

examples.en: Our class checks whether the coverage analysis explains which public statements were quoted in the fictional articles.
examples.zh: 全班核对「媒体报道分析」是否说明虚构文章引用了哪些公开声明。

words.enDefinition: How noticeable a topic or organisation is within coverage, such as whether it appears in the headline or only briefly.

examples.en: The fictional report assesses coverage prominence by distinguishing headline references from brief mentions in the body text.
examples.zh: 虚构报告区分标题提及与正文中的简短提及，以评估「报道中的显著程度」。

examples.en: Our class compares coverage prominence across two fictional articles that discuss the same university reading programme.
examples.zh: 全班比较两篇讨论同一大学阅读项目的虚构文章中的「报道中的显著程度」。

words.enDefinition: A qualitative assessment of how media coverage presents a subject, such as favourably, neutrally, or critically.

examples.en: The fictional evaluation considers coverage tone separately from the number of articles mentioning the campus exhibition.
examples.zh: 虚构评估分别考虑「媒体报道的语气倾向」和提及校园展览的文章数量。

examples.en: Our class discusses coverage tone after comparing two fictional reports that describe the same event differently.
examples.zh: 全班对照两份以不同方式描述同一活动的虚构报道，然后讨论「媒体报道的语气倾向」。

words.enDefinition: The count of relevant media items in a specified set of outlets or reporting period.

examples.en: The fictional evaluation compares coverage volume before and after the launch of a weekend community reading programme.
examples.zh: 虚构评估比较周末社区阅读项目推出前后的「报道数量」。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks whether duplicated articles are included in coverage volume for the fictional reporting period in question.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，虚构报告期的「报道数量」是否纳入重复发表的文章。

words.enDefinition: a document guiding creative work by specifying the intended audience, message, and tone

examples.en: The creative brief asked the writers to use plain language and a warm tone.
examples.zh: 「创意简报」要求文案人员用简明语言和亲切语气。

examples.en: Our designer used the creative brief to check that each sketch communicated the central message.
examples.zh: 设计师根据「创意简报」检查每份草图是否传达了核心信息。

words.enDefinition: a central creative idea that can be expressed in different advertisements or formats

examples.en: The creative concept focused on the small rituals that made a neighborhood shop feel familiar.
examples.zh: 「创意构想」围绕那些让社区小店显得亲切的小习惯。

examples.en: The team presented one creative concept as both a radio script and a poster sketch.
examples.zh: 团队用一份电台稿和一张海报草图呈现同一个「创意构想」。

words.enDefinition: the concrete way an advertising idea is realized in imagery, wording, sound, or format

examples.en: One creative execution used stop-motion animation to show how the pieces fit together.
examples.zh: 其中一种「创意呈现方式」用定格动画展示各零件怎样拼合。

examples.en: The designer kept the main idea and proposed a different creative execution for print readers.
examples.zh: 设计师保留核心构想，给纸媒读者设计了另一种「创意呈现方式」。

words.enDefinition: the practice of cycling through multiple advertising versions across repeated placement opportunities

examples.en: The planner used creative rotation so the digital notice displayed three different images during the campaign.
examples.zh: 规划人员安排「广告素材轮播」，让电子公告在活动期间展示三张不同的图片。

examples.en: The report compared creative rotation with a single design used throughout the same period.
examples.zh: 报告比较同一时期的「广告素材轮播」和始终使用一个设计的方案。

words.enDefinition: one version of an advertisement that changes selected elements for comparison or adaptation

examples.en: The team introduced a creative variation with a shorter headline and the same product image.
examples.zh: 团队推出一个「广告创意版本」，缩短了标题并保留同一产品图。

examples.en: Each creative variation showed the same event details, so the instructor focused on tone and imagery.
examples.zh: 每个「广告创意版本」都展示相同的活动信息，老师主要看语气和图像。

words.enDefinition: a decline in an advertisement's effectiveness after repeated exposure to the same creative material

examples.en: The class discussed creative wearout after repeat viewers paid less attention to the same comedy spot.
examples.zh: 反复观看的观众对同一滑稽短广告注意力变弱后，课堂讨论了「广告创意衰退」。

examples.en: The report tested for creative wearout by comparing responses at similar placements over several weeks.
examples.zh: 报告比较了相似投放位置上几周的反应，检验有无「广告创意衰退」。

words.enDefinition: Communication during and around a serious disruption, intended to inform affected people and explain the organisation's response.

examples.en: The seminar introduces crisis communication with a fictional university maintaining public updates during an extended venue closure.
examples.zh: 研讨课借虚构大学在场地长期关闭期间持续向公众通报的例子，介绍「危机沟通」。

examples.en: Our casebook discusses crisis communication by comparing what was confirmed in the first and later fictional statements.
examples.zh: 案例教材对照第一份和后续虚构声明中已经确认的内容，讨论「危机沟通」。

words.enDefinition: A plan assigning communication roles, information checks, and arrangements for reaching affected groups during a serious disruption.

examples.en: The fictional crisis communication plan specifies who will confirm the facts before issuing a notice about venue availability.
examples.zh: 虚构「危机沟通预案」规定，发布场地能否使用的通知之前，由谁确认事实。

examples.en: Our classroom exercise asks whether the crisis communication plan identifies how affected readers would receive the updates.
examples.zh: 课堂练习询问，「危机沟通预案」是否说明受影响的读者将怎样收到后续通报。

words.enDefinition: A rehearsal that tests how a team would communicate in a hypothetical disruption or emergency.

examples.en: The fictional university runs a crisis communications exercise based on a prolonged closure of a campus reading room.
examples.zh: 虚构大学开展一场以校园阅览室长时间关闭为背景的「危机沟通演练」。

examples.en: Our worksheet lists the facts available at the start of the crisis communications exercise for participants to review.
examples.zh: 练习单列出「危机沟通演练」开始时可获得的事实，供参与者阅读。

collocations: findings from a crisis communications exercise

words.enDefinition: The group assigned to coordinate reliable communication with affected people and the media during a serious disruption.

examples.en: The fictional crisis communications team includes staff who can verify programme dates before publishing public updates.
examples.zh: 虚构「危机沟通团队」的成员中，有人可以在发布公众通报前核实项目日期。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks how the crisis communications team worked with the office responsible for the venue's reopening.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，「危机沟通团队」怎样与负责场地重新开放的部门合作。

collocations: responsibilities of a crisis communications team

words.enDefinition: Transferring incoming goods to outbound transport with little or no storage

examples.en: The warehouse model uses cross-docking to move incoming goods straight to outbound vehicles.
examples.zh: 仓库模型采用「越库转运」，将到货直接转到出库车辆。

examples.en: We discussed cross-docking after identifying which shipments bypassed long-term storage in the case.
examples.zh: 我们辨认出案例中哪些货物无需长期入库后，讨论了「越库转运」。

words.enDefinition: A graph of the total number or share of adopters reached over time.

examples.en: The cumulative adoption curve flattened as fewer new users appeared in the later weeks of the simulation.
examples.zh: 模拟进行到后几周时，新用户变少，「累计采用曲线」趋于平缓。

examples.en: We drew a cumulative adoption curve from the fictional user counts recorded each week on campus.
examples.zh: 我们根据校园中每周记录的虚构用户数画出「累计采用曲线」。

words.enDefinition: Price reduction based on purchases accumulated over a specified period

examples.en: The fictional supplier calculates a cumulative quantity discount based on all orders during the term.
examples.zh: 虚构供应商根据整个约定期间的所有订单计算「累计数量折扣」。

examples.en: We discussed why the cumulative quantity discount was based on several transactions together.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「累计数量折扣」为什么要综合多笔交易来计算。

collocations: qualify for a cumulative quantity discount

words.enDefinition: Research designed for a particular client's questions and information needs.

examples.en: The exercise contrasts custom market research for one fictional supplier with a report available to many subscribers.
examples.zh: 练习把对某个虚构供应商的「定制市场调研」与可供许多订阅者获取的报告相对照。

examples.en: Our case uses custom market research to answer questions unique to the fictional campus shop's product category.
examples.zh: 案例用「定制市场调研」回答虚构校园商店这一产品品类特有的问题。

words.enDefinition: The difference in customer response attributable to what they know about a brand.

examples.en: The case compared responses to identical products with and without names to illustrate customer-based brand equity.
examples.zh: 案例比较了受众对同一款产品在有无品牌名时的反应，以说明「顾客视角的品牌资产」。

examples.en: We discussed customer-based brand equity when students judged two identical fictional offers differently after seeing their names.
examples.zh: 学生看见名称后对两个完全相同的虚构产品作出不同评价，我们就此讨论了「顾客视角的品牌资产」。

collocations: a model of customer-based brand equity

words.enDefinition: Shot temporarily shifting attention away from the scene's main action

examples.en: The class film uses a cutaway shot of the library clock during the conversation.
examples.zh: 课堂影片在对话中切到图书馆的钟，使用了一个「切离镜头」。

examples.en: We reviewed where the cutaway shot interrupts the scene before returning to the speakers.
examples.zh: 我们查看「切离镜头」在画面回到说话者之前从哪处切离当前场景。

words.enDefinition: Production record summarizing work completed and relevant activity on a shooting day

examples.en: The daily production report notes that the crew completed one scene and postponed another.
examples.zh: 「每日拍摄报告」记录摄制组完成了一场戏，推迟了另一场。

examples.en: We used the daily production report to compare planned work with what actually happened.
examples.zh: 我们用「每日拍摄报告」对比计划内的工作和实际完成的情况。

words.enDefinition: A qualification explaining a limitation that affects interpretation of reported data.

examples.en: The article included a data caveat explaining that one branch had recorded only weekday visitors.
examples.zh: 报道附上了「数据使用限制说明」，解释有一家分馆只记录了工作日访客。

examples.en: We wrote a data caveat after realizing that the figures omitted all evening workshop sessions.
examples.zh: 我们意识到这组数字遗漏了所有晚间工作坊，于是写了「数据使用限制说明」。

words.enDefinition: An individual news story whose main findings or structure come from data analysis.

examples.en: The student wrote a data-driven story after noticing that evening library visits rose in the monthly totals.
examples.zh: 学生在每月统计中注意到晚间图书馆到访量上升，写出了一篇「以数据为主线的报道」。

examples.en: We backed up the data-driven story with interviews that helped explain the pattern in public figures.
examples.zh: 我们为「以数据为主线的报道」补充采访，帮助解释公开数据中的变化规律。

words.enDefinition: Reporting that uses quantitative or structured information as evidence to find and explain stories.

examples.en: The data journalism class studied how public library attendance changed across branches during the same period.
examples.zh: 「数据新闻」课研究了同一时期各图书馆分馆的到访量如何变化。

examples.en: We used data journalism to identify which days had the largest changes in the fictional shuttle records.
examples.zh: 我们用「数据新闻」方法从虚构接驳车记录里找出变化最大的几天。

words.enDefinition: The documented approach used to collect, check, and interpret data for a news report.

examples.en: The editor reviewed the data reporting methodology before approving comparisons among the different fictional library branches.
examples.zh: 编辑先审查「数据报道方法」，再批准对不同虚构图书馆分馆作比较。

examples.en: We described our data reporting methodology so classmates could understand how the attendance figures were chosen.
examples.zh: 我们描述了「数据报道方法」，让同学明白所用的到场人数数据是怎样选出来的。

words.enDefinition: A line at the start of a news report identifying its place of origin and sometimes its date.

examples.en: The dateline named the town where the reporter gathered the information for the local transport story.
examples.zh: 「新闻电头」标出了记者为当地交通报道采集信息的城镇。

examples.en: Our editor checked the dateline before publication because the story drew on reporting from two locations.
examples.zh: 因为稿件取材于两个地点的采访，编辑在发表前核对了「新闻电头」。

collocations: a dateline at the start of a report

words.enDefinition: Release making a film available on different platforms on the same date

examples.en: The case uses a day-and-date release for cinema showings and online rental.
examples.zh: 案例将影院放映与网上租看安排为「跨渠道同日发行」。

examples.en: We identified a day-and-date release by comparing the two dates in the release plan.
examples.zh: 我们对照发行方案里的两个日期，辨认出这是「跨渠道同日发行」。

collocations: compare a day-and-date release with separate windows

words.enDefinition: US production schedule showing each cast member's work status across shooting days

examples.en: The day out of days shows when each performer starts, works, and finishes the shoot.
examples.zh: 「演员按日工作表」显示各位演员何时开始、工作和结束拍摄。

examples.en: We checked the day out of days to see which actor was free on Friday.
examples.zh: 我们查看「演员按日工作表」，了解哪位演员周五有空。

collocations: prepare a day out of days
cast listed on the day out of days

words.enDefinition: Defined portion of the broadcast day used for scheduling or audience analysis

examples.en: The sample schedule groups programmes by daypart instead of listing them alphabetically.
examples.zh: 样例排期按「日内播出时段」给节目分组，没有按字母顺序排列。

examples.en: We compared the channel's afternoon audience with that of a later daypart.
examples.zh: 我们将同一频道的下午受众与较晚「日内播出时段」的受众作了比较。

words.enDefinition: scheduling advertising by designated time blocks within a day

examples.en: The planner used dayparting to place the radio advertisement during morning and afternoon travel hours.
examples.zh: 规划人员通过「分时段投放」，把电台广告安排在上午和下午的出行时段。

examples.en: The study compared dayparting by looking at two otherwise similar schedules with different evening allocations.
examples.zh: 研究通过对比两份只有晚间配额不同的排期，比较「分时段投放」安排。

words.enDefinition: The life-cycle stage when sales show a sustained downward trend.

examples.en: The graph marked the decline stage after the fictional calculator's sales fell for three consecutive years.
examples.zh: 图中虚构计算器销量连续三年下降后，这一段被标为「衰退期」。

examples.en: The class discussed whether one unusually slow month was enough to identify the decline stage.
examples.zh: 全班讨论，单凭生意异常清淡的一个月，是否足以判断产品进入「衰退期」。

collocations: manage a product in the decline stage

words.enDefinition: Explicitly chose not to provide a statement in response to a reporter's question.

examples.en: The organizer declined to comment on the proposal after the reporter asked about the revised date.
examples.zh: 记者就提案中修改后的日期提问时，组织人员「明确拒绝置评」。

examples.en: The copy editor wrote declined to comment only after confirming that the person had actively refused.
examples.zh: 文字编辑确认当事人主动拒绝后，才使用「明确拒绝置评」的说法。

collocations: declined to comment on the proposal

words.enDefinition: An agreed interview arrangement allowing information to be used without any attribution.

examples.en: The worksheet explained that information shared on deep background could be reported without attribution to the speaker.
examples.zh: 习题说明，「可用但不注明来源」约定允许报道所提供的信息，无须指明谁提供了消息。

examples.en: The instructor compared deep background with an arrangement that allowed the publication to describe the source.
examples.zh: 老师把「可用但不注明来源」与允许媒体描述来源身份的约定作比较。

words.enDefinition: An opening that sets a scene or creates interest before stating the central news point later.

examples.en: The feature used a delayed lead to set the scene before revealing why the afternoon workshop mattered.
examples.zh: 专题采用「延宕式导语」先交代现场，再点明下午这场工作坊为什么值得报道。

examples.en: Our class compared a delayed lead with an opening that stated the council's decision immediately.
examples.zh: 课堂把「延宕式导语」与直接开头交代委员会决定的写法作比较。

collocations: a feature with a delayed lead

words.enDefinition: Required technical characteristics for supplied screen media files and related material

examples.en: The fictional distributor's delivery specification lists file formats and required audio tracks.
examples.zh: 虚构发行商的「交付技术规范」列出了文件格式和必需音轨。

examples.en: We checked the delivery specification before choosing a file format for the master.
examples.zh: 我们先查看「交付技术规范」，再为母版选择文件格式。

words.enDefinition: Dividing a market by relevant population characteristics described in demographic categories.

examples.en: The teaching example illustrates demographic segmentation using aggregated counts for broad categories in a fictional population table.
examples.zh: 教学示例用虚构人口表中宽泛类别的汇总人数说明「人口统计细分」。

examples.en: Our worksheet discusses demographic segmentation separately from grouping consumers by their reasons for choosing a product.
examples.zh: 练习单分别说明「人口统计细分」和按消费者选产品的原因分组。

words.enDefinition: advertising that shows a product or service in use to make its capabilities apparent

examples.en: The store used demonstration advertising to show how the lamp folds flat for storage.
examples.zh: 商店用「演示式广告」展示了如何把灯折平收起。

examples.en: Our class evaluated demonstration advertising by checking whether the sample video revealed the product's promised function.
examples.zh: 课程让我们检查样片是否展示了商品承诺的功能，以评估「演示式广告」。

words.enDefinition: Checking what total or population underlies a displayed rate, share, or percentage.

examples.en: The denominator check showed that the article's percentage referred only to visitors who answered the survey.
examples.zh: 「分母核对」发现，文章中的百分比仅以回答问卷的访客为基数。

examples.en: Our editor requested a denominator check before comparing percentages from two campus branches with different reporting coverage.
examples.zh: 两家校园分馆的数据统计范围不同，编辑要求先做「分母核对」，再对比两处的百分比。

collocations: a denominator check for a percentage

words.enDefinition: A person formally chosen to speak on a particular topic or on behalf of an organisation.

examples.en: The announcement identifies a designated spokesperson for the fictional college's questions about changes to campus access.
examples.zh: 公告为虚构大学有关校园出入变动的问题指明了一位「指定发言人」。

examples.en: Our worksheet explains why the designated spokesperson handles requests for an official comment in the fictional example.
examples.zh: 练习单解释，在虚构示例中为何由「指定发言人」处理正式置评请求。

words.enDefinition: A product characteristic that meaningfully influences buyers' choice among competing options.

examples.en: Easy carrying became a determinant attribute once students chose repeatedly between cases of different weights.
examples.zh: 学生在不同重量的收纳盒中反复作选择时，便携性成为一项「决定性产品属性」。

examples.en: We tested whether color was a determinant attribute or merely something students liked in all versions.
examples.zh: 我们测试颜色究竟是「决定性产品属性」，还是仅仅在各个版本里都受学生喜欢。

collocations: compare offers on a determinant attribute

words.enDefinition: A news story about a situation whose relevant facts are still emerging.

examples.en: The bus route proposal remained a developing story because the council had yet to publish its timetable.
examples.zh: 公交路线提案仍是「持续发展的新闻」，因为委员会尚未公布时间表。

examples.en: We distinguished confirmed facts from missing details when updating the developing story in our classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 在课堂练习中更新「持续发展的新闻」时，我们区分了已确认的事实和仍待了解的细节。

words.enDefinition: Producer who develops screen ideas and helps shape projects before production

examples.en: The development producer helps the student team turn a concept into a pitch.
examples.zh: 「开发制片人」帮助学生团队把构想整理成可提报的方案。

examples.en: Our case follows a development producer who reshapes the proposed series with the writers.
examples.zh: 案例讲的是一位「开发制片人」与编剧一起调整拟制作剧集的过程。

collocations: pitch an idea to a development producer

words.enDefinition: Group of screen projects a production organization is currently developing

examples.en: The fictional studio adds a short series to its development slate this term.
examples.zh: 虚构工作室本学期将一部短剧加入「开发中项目清单」。

examples.en: We compared the projects on the development slate before reading their individual budgets.
examples.zh: 我们先比较「开发中项目清单」上的项目，再阅读各自的预算。

words.enDefinition: Separate audio submix containing the dialogue components of a larger soundtrack

examples.en: The editor checks the dialogue stem before combining it with the other audio stems.
examples.zh: 剪辑师在合并其他声音分轨之前，先检查了「对白分轨」。

examples.en: We compared the dialogue stem with the full mix to isolate the dialogue.
examples.zh: 我们对照「对白分轨」和全混音，以便单独听取对白。

words.enDefinition: Positioning an offering around a distinctive quality or benefit customers value.

examples.en: The project used differentiation positioning by presenting the fictional notebook as especially suited to sketches and diagrams.
examples.zh: 项目采用「差异化定位」，将虚构笔记本定位为特别适合速写和画示意图的产品。

examples.en: We chose differentiation positioning after finding that rivals all emphasized the same familiar study features.
examples.zh: 发现竞争产品都突出同样常见的学习功能后，我们选择了「差异化定位」。

words.enDefinition: The spread of an innovation through a population over time.

examples.en: The lecture illustrated the diffusion of innovations by tracing use of a fictional note-sharing tool across campuses.
examples.zh: 老师追踪一款虚构笔记分享工具在不同校园的使用情况，以说明「创新扩散」。

examples.en: We used the diffusion of innovations model to discuss why groups adopted the product at different times.
examples.zh: 我们用「创新扩散」模型讨论，为什么不同群体开始用产品的时间不同。

collocations: a model of the diffusion of innovations
factors affecting the diffusion of innovations

words.enDefinition: Standardized collection of digital files prepared for compatible cinema projection systems

examples.en: The venue asks for a digital cinema package to screen the student film.
examples.zh: 放映场地要求提供一套「数字影院放映包」来放映学生影片。

examples.en: We checked whether the digital cinema package included the correct version of the subtitles.
examples.zh: 我们检查了「数字影院放映包」是否包含正确版本的字幕。

words.enDefinition: On-set camera specialist supporting image quality and the digital capture workflow

examples.en: The digital imaging technician checks that the reference look is applied consistently across both cameras.
examples.zh: 「数字影像技师」检查两台摄像机是否统一使用同一种参考画面基调。

examples.en: Our tutor showed where the digital imaging technician fits in the on-set image workflow.
examples.zh: 老师展示了「数字影像技师」在现场影像工作流程中所处的环节。

collocations: work with a digital imaging technician
duties of a digital imaging technician

words.enDefinition: Online spaces where shoppers find, compare, and view products for sale

examples.en: The fictional retailer shows a product's pictures and details on its digital shelf.
examples.zh: 虚构零售商在「数字货架」上展示产品的图片和详细信息。

examples.en: Our group compared the digital shelf with the display in the physical store.
examples.zh: 我们组比较了「数字货架」和实体店里的商品陈列。

collocations: product visibility on the digital shelf

words.enDefinition: A business or product offering a closely comparable solution to the same customers.

examples.en: The second notebook maker was a direct competitor because it sold a similar product to campus buyers.
examples.zh: 第二家笔记本制造商向校园买家卖类似商品，因此是「直接竞争者」。

examples.en: We included a direct competitor on the map to show how buyers compared two reusable planners.
examples.zh: 我们在图上纳入一家「直接竞争者」，展示买家如何比较两款可重复使用的计划本。

words.enDefinition: Distribution from producers to end users without independent sales intermediaries

examples.en: In the case, direct distribution lets the maker sell straight to local libraries.
examples.zh: 在案例中，「直接分销」使生产商能够直接向当地各图书馆销售。

examples.en: We compared direct distribution with a route that includes a regional distributor.
examples.zh: 我们对照了「直接分销」与经过区域分销商的销售路径。

words.enDefinition: advertising designed to prompt a specific, measurable action soon after a recipient sees or hears it

examples.en: The organization used direct-response advertising to ask listeners to call and request a printed workshop schedule.
examples.zh: 机构通过「直接回应广告」，请听众打电话索取印刷的工作坊日程。

examples.en: Our class compared direct-response advertising with an image campaign built around long-term awareness.
examples.zh: 课堂比较了「直接回应广告」和以长期认知为目标的形象宣传活动。

words.enDefinition: Supplier delivery to retail stores without passing through the retailer's distribution center

examples.en: The case uses direct store delivery for goods that bypass the retailer's central warehouse.
examples.zh: 案例对不经零售商中央仓库的货物采用「直送门店」。

examples.en: We traced direct store delivery from the supplier to the shelves in our exercise.
examples.zh: 我们在练习中追踪了从供应商到货架的「直送门店」流程。

words.enDefinition: Crew leader shaping a production's visual photography with the director

examples.en: The director of photography and director agree on a visual look for the library scene.
examples.zh: 「摄影指导」与导演就图书馆场景的画面风格达成一致。

examples.en: We asked the director of photography how the two interiors would look visually distinct.
examples.zh: 我们问「摄影指导」，两个室内场景怎样在视觉上加以区分。

words.enDefinition: Retail outlet emphasizing low prices, usually with relatively limited service

examples.en: The case describes a discount store selling basic products with minimal personal assistance.
examples.zh: 案例描述了一家销售基本商品、很少提供专人协助的「折扣商店」。

examples.en: We discussed the fixed costs of the discount store in the classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂练习中讨论了「折扣商店」的固定成本。

words.enDefinition: Removal of an intermediary stage from an established distribution route

examples.en: The example shows disintermediation when the publisher bypasses its former distributor.
examples.zh: 示例中，出版商绕过原先的分销商，体现了「去中介化」。

examples.en: We compared the two channel diagrams to see where disintermediation occurred.
examples.zh: 我们对比了两幅渠道示意图，查看「去中介化」发生在哪个环节。

words.zhGloss: 任一项达标即可的决策规则
words.enDefinition: A rule accepting an option if it reaches a specified threshold on at least one selected attribute.
acceptedZhAnswers: 任一项达标即可的决策规则

examples.en: The fictional buyer follows a disjunctive decision rule by accepting bags that excel in size or durability.
examples.zh: 虚构买家按照「任一项达标即可的决策规则」，只要包的尺寸或耐用性有一个表现突出就接受。

examples.en: Our tutor demonstrates a disjunctive decision rule using two independent ways for a fictional option to qualify.
examples.zh: 老师用虚构选项的两条独立达标途径演示「任一项达标即可的决策规则」。

collocations: example of a disjunctive decision rule

words.enDefinition: online visual advertising placed on digital pages or in applications

examples.en: The library chose display advertising because it wanted readers to see photographs of the renovated building.
examples.zh: 图书馆选择了「展示广告」，希望读者能看到翻修后的馆舍照片。

examples.en: The agency ran display advertising on several websites frequented by readers of local arts news.
examples.zh: 机构在本地艺术新闻读者常访问的几家网站上投放了「展示广告」。

words.zhGloss: 希望保持距离的参照群体
words.enDefinition: A group a person prefers not to resemble or be associated with.
acceptedZhAnswers: 希望保持距离的参照群体

examples.en: The seminar uses a fictional campus event to discuss what it means to have a dissociative reference group.
examples.zh: 研讨课借一场虚构校园活动，讨论拥有一个「希望保持距离的参照群体」意味着什么。

examples.en: The fictional shopper describes a dissociative reference group whose style they would prefer to avoid resembling.
examples.zh: 虚构购物者描述一个「希望保持距离的参照群体」，并表示不想自己的风格和这群人相似。

collocations: example of a dissociative reference group
avoid association with a dissociative reference group

words.zhGloss: 减少失调感的购买行为
words.enDefinition: In a marketing framework, high-involvement buying when the consumer sees little difference among available alternatives and may later seek reassurance.
acceptedZhAnswers: 减少失调感的购买行为

examples.en: The case compares dissonance-reducing buying behavior with another fictional purchase involving several clearly different alternatives.
examples.zh: 案例把「减少失调感的购买行为」与另一项有几个明显不同备选项的虚构购买相比较。

examples.en: Our worksheet links dissonance-reducing buying behavior to a fictional choice the student considers important despite similar alternatives.
examples.zh: 练习单将「减少失调感的购买行为」与虚构学生尽管面对相似备选项、仍认为很重要的选择联系起来。

words.enDefinition: System coordinating order fulfillment across multiple sources of inventory or service

examples.en: The model uses distributed order management to coordinate orders across two warehouses and several shops.
examples.zh: 模型利用「分布式订单管理」在两个仓库和几家商店之间协调订单。

examples.en: We discussed how distributed order management differs from handling orders within a single location.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「分布式订单管理」与仅在一个地点处理订单有何不同。

words.enDefinition: Costs incurred in preparing, marketing, and delivering a title to outlets

examples.en: The mock report lists artwork and file delivery among its distribution expenses.
examples.zh: 模拟报告把宣传图制作和文件交付列入「发行支出」。

examples.en: We distinguished distribution expenses from the fee retained by the distributor in the example.
examples.zh: 我们将「发行支出」与示例中发行商保留的服务费区分开来。

words.enDefinition: Amount paid or retained by a distributor for its distribution services

examples.en: The worksheet lists the distribution fee as a separate deduction from gross receipts.
examples.zh: 习题把「发行服务费」列为总收入中的单独扣除项。

examples.en: We compared the distribution fee across two sample agreements for the same film.
examples.zh: 我们对比同一部影片的两份样本协议中的「发行服务费」。

words.enDefinition: An extension that adds products below the line's existing market tier.

examples.en: The basic lamp represented a downward line stretch for a fictional brand previously selling premium models.
examples.zh: 对之前只卖高端型号的虚构品牌而言，这种基础款台灯是一次「产品线向下延伸」。

examples.en: Students debated whether a downward line stretch would change perceptions of the original desk accessory line.
examples.zh: 学生讨论「产品线向下延伸」会不会改变顾客对原来桌面用品系列的看法。

collocations: risks of a downward line stretch

words.enDefinition: Fulfillment arrangement where a supplier ships goods directly to a retailer's customer

examples.en: The example uses drop shipping so the supplier sends orders directly to customers.
examples.zh: 示例采用「供应商代发货」，由供应商直接将订单商品寄给顾客。

examples.en: We contrasted drop shipping with the retailer stocking and shipping the product itself.
examples.zh: 我们把「供应商代发货」与零售商自行备货发货的做法作了对照。

words.enDefinition: Selling an offering through both direct and intermediary routes in parallel

examples.en: The fictional maker uses dual distribution by selling online and through independent shops.
examples.zh: 虚构生产商既在网上直售，也通过独立商店销售，采用了「双重分销」。

examples.en: We identified dual distribution after tracing the same product through direct and indirect routes.
examples.zh: 我们追查了同一产品经直接与间接路径销售的情况，辨认出了「双重分销」。

words.enDefinition: A physical product intended to last through extended or repeated use.

examples.en: The fictional student counted the desk lamp as a durable good and expected years of use.
examples.zh: 虚构学生将台灯算作「耐用品」，预计能用好几年。

examples.en: Our class compared purchase decisions for a durable good with decisions about goods used up quickly.
examples.zh: 全班把购买「耐用品」时的决策与购买很快就会用完的商品时的决策作比较。

words.enDefinition: The adopter group following early adopters and preceding the midpoint of adoption in the model.

examples.en: In the simulation, the early majority began using the notebook once the first few groups had adopted it.
examples.zh: 模拟中，最初几个小组采用笔记本后，「早期大众」开始使用它。

examples.en: The class located the early majority before the midpoint on the cumulative chart of fictional adopters.
examples.zh: 在虚构采用者累计图上，全班找到了位于中点之前的「早期大众」。

collocations: the early majority in a diffusion model

words.enDefinition: Independent attention or coverage an organisation receives through external media without buying or controlling the placement.

examples.en: The fictional project records earned media when a local newspaper independently reports on its new reading programme.
examples.zh: 当地报纸独立报道虚构项目的新阅读计划，项目记录这项报道为「免费媒体报道」。

examples.en: Our worksheet classifies the newspaper article as earned media because the outlet made its own editorial decision.
examples.zh: 练习单将该报刊文章归为「免费媒体报道」，因为媒体自行作出了编辑决定。

words.enDefinition: Keeping prices low by offering basic features and minimizing costs

examples.en: The fictional stationery brand uses economy pricing for a notebook with basic features.
examples.zh: 虚构文具品牌对功能基本的笔记本采用「经济型定价」。

examples.en: We compared economy pricing with a higher price for a more elaborate product.
examples.zh: 我们将「经济型定价」与为功能更丰富的产品定更高价格的做法作了比较。

collocations: compare economy pricing with premium pricing

words.enDefinition: The senior editor with overall responsibility for a publication's editorial direction.

examples.en: The editor-in-chief approved a new policy on how the student paper would label opinion pieces.
examples.zh: 「总编辑」批准了一项新规定，明确学生报怎样给评论文章加标识。

examples.en: The editorial board sent its proposed coverage priorities to the editor-in-chief before the new term began.
examples.zh: 新学期开始前，编委会把建议优先报道的议题发给了「总编辑」。

words.enDefinition: The group responsible for developing a publication's collective positions on matters addressed in its editorials.

examples.en: The editorial board discussed the student paper's opinion policy before publishing its statement about campus services.
examples.zh: 学生报的「编辑委员会」在发布有关校园服务的声明之前，先讨论了评论版的方针。

examples.en: We asked the editorial board how its collective views were distinguished from those of individual columnists.
examples.zh: 我们问「编辑委员会」，怎样区分委员会集体观点和专栏作者的个人观点。

collocations: a decision by the editorial board

words.enDefinition: A public acknowledgment and repair of a factual error in a published news report.

examples.en: The newsroom issued an editorial correction after learning that the article gave the wrong opening time.
examples.zh: 新闻室得知文章给出的开放时间有误后，发布了「报道事实更正」。

examples.en: We read the editorial correction to see which detail had changed and what the correct information was.
examples.zh: 我们读了「报道事实更正」，看哪项细节改了，以及正确消息是什么。

collocations: an editorial correction to a story

words.enDefinition: Freedom to make editorial decisions without improper outside or commercial pressure.

examples.en: The student paper defended editorial independence when a sponsor asked to approve coverage of the campus festival.
examples.zh: 赞助方要求审定校园活动报道时，学生报维护了「编辑独立性」。

examples.en: We discussed editorial independence by looking at who had final responsibility for the publication's coverage decisions.
examples.zh: 我们查看谁对刊物的报道决定负最终责任，借此讨论「编辑独立性」。

words.enDefinition: A meeting at which editors and reporters plan coverage and discuss stories.

examples.en: At the editorial meeting, student reporters explained which sources they had reached and what remained unconfirmed.
examples.zh: 在「编采会议」上，学生记者说明已经联系了哪些消息来源，还有哪些细节没有确认。

examples.en: The editorial meeting ended with a schedule for the two stories the newsroom wanted by Friday.
examples.zh: 「编采会议」结束时，新闻室定下时间表，要求周五前完成两篇报道。

collocations: bring a pitch to an editorial meeting

words.enDefinition: Openness about how news was gathered, verified, presented, or corrected.

examples.en: The student publication improved editorial transparency by explaining how the public attendance numbers had been collected.
examples.zh: 学生刊物解释了公开到场人数数据的收集方式，提高了「编辑透明度」。

examples.en: We discussed editorial transparency after the newsroom added a readable explanation of its recent correction.
examples.zh: 新闻室为最近一次更正附上易读的说明后，我们讨论了「编辑透明度」。

words.enDefinition: A published message from editors providing context or explaining an editorial decision.

examples.en: An editor's note explained why the student paper had combined two previously separate articles into one.
examples.zh: 「编者按」解释了学生报为何把以前分开的两篇文章合为一篇。

examples.en: We placed the editor's note above the article to explain why the original documents were linked below.
examples.zh: 我们把「编者按」放在文章上方，解释为什么原始文件的链接列在下方。

words.enDefinition: Permission to show a film in specified educational settings or programmes

examples.en: The fictional university discusses educational screening rights before arranging a course screening for students.
examples.zh: 虚构大学先讨论「教育放映权」，再为学生安排课程放映。

examples.en: We marked educational screening rights separately from commercial cinema exhibition in the sample agreement.
examples.zh: 我们在样例协议中把「教育放映权」与商业影院放映分开标出。

words.enDefinition: the chosen or estimated number of exposures needed for a specified advertising response

examples.en: The exercise assumed an effective frequency of three exposures and asked students to compare schedules.
examples.zh: 练习将三次曝光设为「有效曝光频次」，请学生比较投放排期。

examples.en: The planner treated effective frequency as an estimate that might differ across audiences and objectives.
examples.zh: 规划人员把「有效曝光频次」作为估计值，会随受众和目标改变。

words.enDefinition: the audience count or share receiving at least the number of exposures chosen as an effectiveness threshold

examples.en: The planner reported effective reach as the share of listeners who heard the spot at least three times.
examples.zh: 规划人员用至少听到三次广告的听众占比来报告「有效触达」。

examples.en: Two schedules can have the same total reach and differ in effective reach under the selected threshold.
examples.zh: 按照选定的阈值，两套排期的总触达可以相同，「有效触达」也可以不同。

collocations: calculate effective reach at a stated frequency

words.enDefinition: An interview conducted through written questions and answers exchanged by email.

examples.en: The student reporter arranged an email interview because the organizer was unavailable during the newsroom meeting.
examples.zh: 组织人员在新闻室开会时没有空，学生记者就安排了「电子邮件采访」。

examples.en: We followed the email interview with one question asking the organizer to clarify the opening date.
examples.zh: 结束「电子邮件采访」后，我们又问了一个问题，请组织人员明确开幕日期。

words.enDefinition: a persuasive approach based on feelings that the message seeks to evoke

examples.en: The ad used an emotional appeal by showing how old photographs brought a family together.
examples.zh: 这则广告展现老照片怎样让一家人聚在一起，使用了「情感诉求」。

examples.en: The team chose an emotional appeal centered on the pride of completing a first community performance.
examples.zh: 团队选择了「情感诉求」，突出首次完成社区演出的自豪感。

words.enDefinition: A feeling a customer gains from using or owning an offering.

examples.en: The fictional repair kit offered an emotional benefit because students felt more confident tackling small fixes.
examples.zh: 虚构工具套装让学生更有信心应付小修小补，提供了「情感利益」。

examples.en: We discussed the emotional benefit of a familiar welcome page in the case about new students.
examples.zh: 我们在新生案例中讨论了熟悉的欢迎页面带来的「情感利益」。

collocations: connect a feature to an emotional benefit

words.enDefinition: a final graphic or text screen that presents information at the end of a video

examples.en: The end card showed the exhibition dates and the address of the ticket office.
examples.zh: 「片尾信息画面」显示展览日期和售票处地址。

examples.en: The editor held the end card long enough for viewers to read the event details.
examples.zh: 剪辑师保留「片尾信息画面」足够长的时间，以便观众读清活动详情。

words.enDefinition: In-store ordering access to products not physically stocked in that store

examples.en: The mock store uses an endless aisle to offer colors missing from its shelves.
examples.zh: 模拟商店利用「无限货架」提供实体货架上没有的颜色。

examples.en: We discussed how the endless aisle extends the assortment available through the shop.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「无限货架」如何扩大购物者通过门店能买到的商品范围。

words.enDefinition: A distinct brand whose credibility is visibly supported by another brand.

examples.en: The fictional shop treated its notebook label as an endorsed brand by placing its company name below.
examples.zh: 虚构商店在笔记本品牌下方标上公司名称，使其成为「背书式品牌」。

examples.en: Students separated the endorsed brand's name from the small supporting name printed beside it in the example.
examples.zh: 学生区分了示例中的「背书式品牌」名称和印在旁边字号较小的背书方名称。

collocations: display the parent name on an endorsed brand

words.enDefinition: Reporter-initiated coverage that develops an original story beyond routine events or announcements.

examples.en: The enterprise reporting assignment began with questions from readers rather than with a scheduled campus announcement.
examples.zh: 「记者主动策划的报道」作业从读者的提问出发，并非由一次预定的校园公告发起。

examples.en: We discussed enterprise reporting after a reporter connected several small library changes into one original story.
examples.zh: 一名记者把图书馆数项小调整串成一篇原创报道后，我们讨论了「记者主动策划的报道」。

words.enDefinition: Share of eligible viewers or starts meeting an episode's completion criterion

examples.en: The fictional platform states its scoring rule before reporting the episode completion rate.
examples.zh: 虚构平台先说明统计规则，再报告「单集完播率」。

examples.en: We compared the episode completion rate with how many people began watching the episode.
examples.zh: 我们将「单集完播率」与开始观看该集的人数作了比较。

words.enDefinition: The stage in which consumers compare possible options using relevant characteristics or standards.

examples.en: The class illustrates evaluation of alternatives by comparing size, weight, and durability across three fictional notebooks.
examples.zh: 课堂通过比较三种虚构笔记本的尺寸、重量和耐用性来说明「备选方案评估」。

examples.en: Our worksheet places evaluation of alternatives between looking up information and making a final purchase choice.
examples.zh: 练习单把「备选方案评估」放在查询信息和作出最终购买选择之间。

words.enDefinition: Keeping regular prices low and relatively stable with few temporary promotions

examples.en: The case contrasts everyday low pricing with frequent changes between regular and promotional prices.
examples.zh: 案例把「天天低价策略」与经常在常规价和促销价之间切换作了对照。

examples.en: We checked how the mock calendar reflected everyday low pricing during the semester.
examples.zh: 我们查看模拟日历在学期内如何体现「天天低价策略」。

collocations: compare everyday low pricing with promotions

words.enDefinition: A model linking satisfaction to how perceived performance compares with prior expectations.

examples.en: The seminar uses the expectancy disconfirmation model to interpret a fictional student's satisfaction with a recently purchased folder.
examples.zh: 研讨课用「期望不一致模型」解释虚构学生对刚购文件夹的满意程度。

examples.en: Our worksheet applies the expectancy disconfirmation model by comparing fictional reports of expected and experienced product performance.
examples.zh: 练习单比较预期产品表现与实际体验的虚构报告，应用了「期望不一致模型」。

collocations: predictions of the expectancy disconfirmation model

words.enDefinition: The attributes and conditions buyers normally expect with an offering in its category.

examples.en: In the classroom case, clear assembly instructions were part of the expected product for a shelving kit.
examples.zh: 课堂案例中，易懂的安装说明属于搁架套装的「期望产品层」。

examples.en: We discussed whether a secure lid belonged to the expected product in the reusable cup category.
examples.zh: 我们讨论，在可重复使用杯这一品类中，能盖紧的杯盖是否属于「期望产品层」。

collocations: a service included in the expected product

words.enDefinition: An article making a complex topic understandable by answering key questions and supplying context.

examples.en: The student paper published an explainer article about how the new library reservation system would work.
examples.zh: 学生报发了一篇「解释性报道」，说明图书馆新的预约系统如何运作。

examples.en: We built the explainer article around three questions readers had asked after seeing the initial announcement.
examples.zh: 我们围绕读者看过最初公告后提出的三个问题写成了「解释性报道」。

words.enDefinition: the group of people who encounter the advertisement studied in a campaign evaluation

examples.en: The exposed group saw the poster before answering the questionnaire about the exhibition dates.
examples.zh: 「广告曝光组」先看到海报，再回答有关展览日期的问卷。

examples.en: The report compared awareness in the exposed group with awareness among respondents who saw no advertisement.
examples.zh: 报告对照了「广告曝光组」和未看到广告的受访者的认知水平。

collocations: compare the exposed group with a control group

words.zhGloss: 广泛型消费者问题解决
words.enDefinition: A purchase approach involving substantial information search and detailed evaluation of alternatives.
acceptedZhAnswers: 广泛型消费者问题解决

examples.en: The worksheet describes extended consumer problem solving when the fictional student compares several unfamiliar models in detail.
examples.zh: 练习单用虚构学生详细比较几个不熟悉型号的例子来说明「广泛型消费者问题解决」。

examples.en: Our tutor asks whether weeks of information search and evaluation amount to extended consumer problem solving here.
examples.zh: 老师讨论，本例持续数周的信息搜寻和评估是否构成「广泛型消费者问题解决」。

collocations: engage in extended consumer problem solving
example of extended consumer problem solving
demands of extended consumer problem solving

words.enDefinition: How naturally customers think a proposed extension fits its established brand.

examples.en: Students rated extension fit higher when the new product served a familiar purpose for that brand.
examples.zh: 新产品满足的是该品牌原先就让人熟悉的用途时，学生给出的「品牌延伸契合度」评分更高。

examples.en: The case discussed extension fit before comparing customer reactions to the two fictional proposals.
examples.zh: 在比较顾客对两个虚构方案的反应之前，案例先讨论了「品牌延伸契合度」。

words.enDefinition: An organisation's communication with people and groups outside the organisation, including partners, media, and the public.

examples.en: The fictional college puts the notice for neighbouring residents under external communications in its sample plan.
examples.zh: 虚构大学在示例计划里，将发给附近居民的通知归入「对外沟通」。

examples.en: Our class separates external communications about the exhibition from emails sent only to the organising team.
examples.zh: 全班把关于展览的「对外沟通」与只发给组织团队的邮件分开。

words.enDefinition: Looking beyond memory to other people, publicly available material, or product information to inform a consumer decision.

examples.en: The fictional shopper consults a product guide during external information search for an unfamiliar type of folder.
examples.zh: 虚构购物者挑选不熟悉的文件夹时查看产品指南，进行了「外部信息搜寻」。

examples.en: Our reading compares external information search in two fictional purchasing decisions with different levels of familiarity.
examples.zh: 读物比较两项熟悉程度不同的虚构购买决策中的「外部信息搜寻」。

words.enDefinition: Comparison price supplied by an external source such as a displayed price

examples.en: The example labels the displayed comparison amount as an external reference price for shoppers.
examples.zh: 示例把展示出来的对比金额标为购物者的「外在参考价格」。

examples.en: We explained why an external reference price does not come from the buyer's memory.
examples.zh: 我们解释了为什么「外在参考价格」并非来自买家的记忆。

collocations: compare against an external reference price

words.zhGloss: 触发需求识别的外部刺激
words.enDefinition: An environmental or social cue that draws a consumer's attention to a possible unmet need.
acceptedZhAnswers: 触发需求识别的外部刺激

examples.en: The fictional timetable change represents an external stimulus for need recognition when students consider buying earlier meals.
examples.zh: 虚构课表变动促使学生考虑早点买饭，属于一种「触发需求识别的外部刺激」。

examples.en: The class identifies an external stimulus for need recognition in the fictional diary entry about a shared project.
examples.zh: 全班在关于共同项目的虚构日记里，找出一种「触发需求识别的外部刺激」。

collocations: identify an external stimulus for need recognition
example of an external stimulus for need recognition
classify an external stimulus for need recognition

words.enDefinition: Edit following a character's gaze with a shot of what they see

examples.en: The eyeline match cuts from the student's glance to a notebook across the room.
examples.zh: 「视线匹配」剪辑先拍学生望过去，再切到房间另一头的笔记本。

examples.en: We checked the eyeline match before finalizing the cut between the two shots.
examples.zh: 我们在确定两个镜头之间的剪接之前检查了「视线匹配」。

words.enDefinition: A statement describing an event from someone who personally saw it happen.

examples.en: The student reporter compared each eyewitness account of the power cut with the building's published update.
examples.zh: 学生记者将停电的各份「目击者陈述」分别与大楼发布的最新消息作比较。

examples.en: We checked where the observer stood before relying on the eyewitness account in the simulated report.
examples.zh: 在模拟报道中采用这份「目击者陈述」前，我们先核对观察者当时站在什么位置。

words.enDefinition: A newsroom unit that tests factual claims against reliable evidence.

examples.en: The fact-checking desk compared the attendance claim with the public figures and asked about a discrepancy.
examples.zh: 「事实核查组」把有关到场人数的说法与公开数据作比较，并询问两者为何不一致。

examples.en: Our fictional fact-checking desk returned the claim with a note explaining which part lacked supporting evidence.
examples.zh: 虚构「事实核查组」退回了这项说法，并附注说明哪一部分缺少佐证。

collocations: a review by the fact-checking desk
send a claim to the fact-checking desk

words.enDefinition: A published assessment of how well the evidence supports a specific factual claim.

examples.en: The fact-checking verdict explained why the quoted timetable claim was only partly supported by the public records.
examples.zh: 「事实核查结论」解释了为什么公开记录只支持所引时间表说法的一部分。

examples.en: We checked whether the fact-checking verdict referred to the precise claim investigated in the student article.
examples.zh: 我们核对「事实核查结论」所指的是否确实是学生报道调查的那项说法。

words.zhGloss: 供媒体使用的事实要览
words.enDefinition: A short reference sheet listing verified details that journalists can consult about an event, service, or organisation.
acceptedZhAnswers: 供媒体使用的事实要览

examples.en: The fictional fact sheet for the media lists the exhibition dates, venue, and number of participating groups.
examples.zh: 虚构「供媒体使用的事实要览」列出展览日期、场地和参与团体数量。

examples.en: Our worksheet checks whether the totals in the fact sheet for the media match the fictional programme records.
examples.zh: 练习单核对「供媒体使用的事实要览」中的总数与虚构项目记录是否一致。

collocations: publish a fact sheet for the media
verify a fact sheet for the media
details in a fact sheet for the media

words.enDefinition: Retail outlet operated by a manufacturer or brand to sell its goods

examples.en: The fictional clothing producer sells remaining items through its own factory outlet.
examples.zh: 虚构服装生产商通过自己的「工厂直销店」出售余货。

examples.en: We distinguished a manufacturer's factory outlet from a shop that bought excess inventory independently.
examples.zh: 我们把制造商的「工厂直销店」与独立购入过剩库存的商店区分开来。

words.enDefinition: Giving positions equal weight in coverage when the available evidence supports them unequally.

examples.en: The tutor called it false balance when the report weighed an unsupported guess equally with verified records.
examples.zh: 报道同等看待没有依据的猜测与已核实的记录，老师称之为「虚假平衡」。

examples.en: We revised the paragraph to avoid false balance while still identifying which person made the disputed claim.
examples.zh: 我们修改了段落以避免「虚假平衡」，同时明确了有争议的说法出自何人。

words.enDefinition: Viewing copy submitted for a festival's selection process rather than public projection

examples.en: Our group uploaded a festival screener for the fictional student festival selection panel.
examples.zh: 我们组为虚构学生电影节的选片小组上传了「电影节评审看片版」。

examples.en: We distinguished the festival screener from the package prepared for the actual screening.
examples.zh: 我们区分了「电影节评审看片版」与为正式放映准备的放映包。

words.enDefinition: To send a completed news report to an editor or newsroom system.

examples.en: The student reporter planned to file a story once she had checked when the exhibition would open.
examples.zh: 学生记者打算核实展览的开幕时间后再「提交报道稿」。
