examples.en: We included the product platform on the diagram to show which modules the fictional designs shared.
examples.zh: 我们在图中标出「产品平台」，用来展示虚构设计共用的模块。

collocations: build on a shared product platform

words.enDefinition: Defining a product's intended place in customers' minds relative to alternatives.

examples.en: Our product positioning emphasized the compact size of this lamp for students with small shared desks.
examples.zh: 我们的「产品定位」强调这款台灯体积小，适合合用小书桌的学生。

examples.en: We revised the product positioning after classmates described the fictional bag as practical for everyday use.
examples.zh: 同学认为虚构包袋适合日常使用后，我们修改了「产品定位」。

words.enDefinition: Evaluating how a physical or usable version performs under relevant conditions.

examples.en: During product testing, students checked whether the reusable cover still fitted after repeated removal in the simulation.
examples.zh: 在模拟的「产品测试」中，学生检查可重复使用的封皮拆卸多次后是否仍然合适。

examples.en: We compared the product testing notes with earlier opinions about the concept before it had been built.
examples.zh: 我们把「产品测试」记录与实际做出产品前对构想的看法作比较。

words.enDefinition: The frequency or amount of use of a product within a specified period or among a stated group.

examples.en: The sample research report compares product usage rate across three fictional groups during the same stated period.
examples.zh: 研究报告样本比较三个虚构群体在同一规定时段内的「产品使用频率或用量」。

examples.en: Our class asks whether product usage rate in the example refers to number of uses or quantity used.
examples.zh: 全班讨论示例中的「产品使用频率或用量」是指使用次数还是使用数量。

words.enDefinition: Art department worker who sources and arranges purchases or rentals for sets

examples.en: The production buyer arranges a rental for the lamps chosen by the set decorator.
examples.zh: 「影视道具采购员」为布景陈设师选定的灯具安排租赁。

examples.en: We asked the production buyer which furnishings could arrive before the student shoot.
examples.zh: 我们问「影视道具采购员」，哪些陈设能在学生影片开拍前送到。

words.enDefinition: Crew member coordinating production office paperwork, communications, and practical arrangements

examples.en: The production coordinator sends the student crew a reminder about the new meeting point.
examples.zh: 「制片协调员」向学生摄制组发出提醒，告知新的集合地点。

examples.en: We asked the production coordinator where to find the latest schedule for rehearsals.
examples.zh: 我们问「制片协调员」在哪里能找到最新的排练日程。

words.enDefinition: Head of the department shaping the visual world of a screen production

examples.en: The production designer presents sketches of the fictional library before the set is built.
examples.zh: 图书馆布景搭建前，「影视美术指导」展示了场景草图。

examples.en: Our team asked the production designer how the two locations might share a palette.
examples.zh: 我们组问「影视美术指导」，怎样让两个地点采用相同的配色。

words.enDefinition: Crew member overseeing the recording of dialogue and other sound during filming

examples.en: The production sound mixer hears a chair scrape just before the actor's line.
examples.zh: 「现场录音师」在演员说台词前听到了椅子的刮擦声。

examples.en: Our crew asked the production sound mixer which take had the clearest dialogue.
examples.zh: 我们摄制组问「现场录音师」，哪一条里的对白最清楚。

collocations: work with the production sound mixer
notes from the production sound mixer

words.enDefinition: Setting prices primarily to reach a profit or return goal

examples.en: The report uses profit-oriented pricing to compare scenarios with the same expected sales volume.
examples.zh: 报告用「利润导向定价」比较预期销量相同的几个情境。

examples.en: We discussed profit-oriented pricing when the fictional firm gave earnings priority over growth.
examples.zh: 虚构公司将收益置于增长之上时，我们讨论了「利润导向定价」。

collocations: contrast profit-oriented pricing with sales targets

words.enDefinition: Programme scheduled immediately before another, potentially drawing viewers into the following show

examples.en: The scheduler chooses a programme lead-in that might bring viewers to the new drama.
examples.zh: 排期员选择了一档可能为新剧带来观众的「前导节目」。

examples.en: We reviewed the programme lead-in before explaining the audience pattern for the later show.
examples.zh: 解释后一档节目的受众分布之前，我们先查看其「前导节目」。

words.enDefinition: Number or proportion of distinct viewers meeting a programme's stated viewing criterion

examples.en: The classroom table counts each eligible viewer only once when estimating programme reach.
examples.zh: 课堂表格在估计「节目收视触达」时，每位符合条件的观众只计一次。

examples.en: We checked the minimum viewing rule used for programme reach in the fictional report.
examples.zh: 我们查看虚构报告对「节目收视触达」采用了怎样的最低观看要求。

words.enDefinition: the combination of advertising, sales promotion, public relations and other tools used to communicate with a market

examples.en: The gallery added educator outreach to its promotion mix before announcing the new exhibition.
examples.zh: 美术馆宣布新展之前，把面向教育工作者的联络纳入了「促销组合」。

examples.en: The class compared the promotion mix of a campus store with that of a subscription service.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们比较校园商店与订阅服务的「促销组合」。

words.enDefinition: Short film made to demonstrate the potential of a proposed screen project

examples.en: The students made a proof-of-concept short to show how the imagined world might look.
examples.zh: 学生制作了「概念验证短片」，展示构想中的世界会是什么样。

examples.en: The proof-of-concept short helped classmates understand the tone of the proposed feature.
examples.zh: 「概念验证短片」帮助同学理解了拟拍长片的基调。

words.enDefinition: Lightweight copies of source files used to make editing more manageable

examples.en: The student editor uses proxy media because the source files are too large.
examples.zh: 源文件太大，学生剪辑师改用「剪辑代理素材」工作。

examples.en: We checked that the proxy media matched the timing of the original clips.
examples.zh: 我们检查了「剪辑代理素材」是否与原始片段保持相同时间对应关系。

words.enDefinition: Dividing a market by shared lifestyles, values, interests, or similar characteristics rather than solely by demographics.

examples.en: The course illustrates psychographic segmentation with fictional profiles that differ in their reported leisure interests and activities.
examples.zh: 课程用在自报休闲兴趣与活动上有所不同的虚构画像说明「心理特征细分」。

examples.en: Our seminar compares psychographic segmentation with a classification based only on region in the same fictional example.
examples.zh: 研讨课把「心理特征细分」与在同一虚构示例中仅依据地区作的分类相比。

words.enDefinition: Setting or presenting prices to influence how buyers perceive those prices

examples.en: The tutorial examines psychological pricing by asking how people interpret two nearby prices.
examples.zh: 辅导课通过询问人们如何理解两个相近价位来考察「心理定价」。

examples.en: We discussed psychological pricing without assuming that everyone reacts to prices the same way.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「心理定价」，没有假定每个人对价格的反应都一样。

words.enDefinition: Work involving an organisation's relationships and communication with public institutions and groups concerned with public policy.

examples.en: The course introduces public affairs through a fictional university discussing library access with a local council.
examples.zh: 课程用虚构大学与地方议会讨论图书馆开放范围的例子介绍「公共事务沟通」。

examples.en: Our casebook distinguishes public affairs from advertising an event to prospective visitors in the same fictional project.
examples.zh: 案例教材将「公共事务沟通」与同一虚构项目中向潜在访客宣传活动区分开来。

words.enDefinition: Coverage of government bodies, public institutions, and decisions affecting a community.

examples.en: The public affairs reporting exercise asked students to explain how a council decision changed local library hours.
examples.zh: 「公共事务报道」练习要求学生说明，某项委员会决定怎样改变了当地图书馆的开放时间。

examples.en: We used a public meeting summary to practice public affairs reporting with clearly attributed statements.
examples.zh: 我们用一份公开会议摘要练习「公共事务报道」，并清楚标明每项说法的来源。

collocations: a course in public affairs reporting
public affairs reporting on local services

words.enDefinition: A coordinated effort intended to make a defined audience more aware of an issue, organisation, or service.

examples.en: The fictional public awareness campaign tells residents that the university library offers a public reading area on weekends.
examples.zh: 虚构「公众认知宣传活动」告诉居民，大学图书馆周末设有公众阅览区。

examples.en: Our class assesses the public awareness campaign by comparing synthetic awareness measures from before and after the project.
examples.zh: 全班通过比较项目前后的合成认知度指标来评估「公众认知宣传活动」。

collocations: objective of a public awareness campaign

words.enDefinition: Communication by an organisation with members of the public about its activities, decisions, or services.

examples.en: The casebook introduces public communications through a fictional college sharing information about changes to community access.
examples.zh: 案例教材以虚构大学公布社区使用权限变化为例，介绍「公众沟通」。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks which documents count as public communications when the fictional university closes a study space.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，虚构大学关闭一处自习空间时，哪些文件属于「公众沟通」。

words.enDefinition: A process in which an organisation or public body invites public views on a proposal or decision under consideration.

examples.en: The fictional council begins a public consultation on proposed changes to the local reading room's weekend hours.
examples.zh: 虚构地方议会就调整本地阅览室周末时段的提议启动「公开征询意见」。

examples.en: Our class asks which options were still open for discussion during the public consultation in the sample timeline.
examples.zh: 全班询问，在样本时间线里的「公开征询意见」期间，哪些选项仍供讨论。

words.enDefinition: The involvement of members of the public through activities such as discussion, consultation, or contribution to a project.

examples.en: The casebook uses public engagement to describe the fictional library's opportunities for residents to contribute ideas.
examples.zh: 案例教材用「公众参与」来描述虚构图书馆让居民提供想法的机会。

examples.en: Our seminar discusses public engagement after reviewing the participation summary for the fictional university's exhibition project.
examples.zh: 研讨课阅读虚构大学展览项目的参与情况摘要后，讨论了「公众参与」。

words.zhGloss: 面向公众的常见问题解答
words.enDefinition: A set of published answers to common questions intended for people outside the organisation.
acceptedZhAnswers: 面向公众的常见问题解答

examples.en: The fictional library publishes a public-facing FAQ about temporary opening hours alongside its longer notice to visitors.
examples.zh: 虚构图书馆在较长的访客通知旁，发布一份关于临时开放时间的「面向公众的常见问题解答」。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks whether the public-facing FAQ explains how readers can reach the replacement study space easily.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，「面向公众的常见问题解答」是否说明读者如何方便地到达替代自习空间。

words.enDefinition: Coordinated communication intended to give the public practical information about an issue, change, or service.

examples.en: The fictional library runs a public information campaign explaining how readers can use its temporary study space.
examples.zh: 虚构图书馆开展「公众信息传播活动」，说明读者怎样使用临时自习空间。

examples.en: Our casebook connects the public information campaign to the practical questions residents asked in the sample feedback.
examples.zh: 案例教材把「公众信息传播活动」与居民在反馈样本里提出的实际问题联系起来。

words.enDefinition: An official responsible for providing accurate information to the public and media on behalf of an organisation or agency.

examples.en: The casebook lists the public information officer as the contact for questions about a fictional community centre closure.
examples.zh: 案例教材把「公众信息专员」列为虚构社区中心关闭问题的联系人。

examples.en: Our class compares the responsibilities of a public information officer with those of the staff preparing internal reports.
examples.zh: 全班把「公众信息专员」的职责与负责编写内部报告的员工职责作比较。

collocations: public information officer for an agency

words.enDefinition: Communication intended to serve public needs or help people understand matters of shared concern.

examples.en: The seminar illustrates public-interest communication with a fictional programme explaining access to a community reading room.
examples.zh: 研讨课以说明如何使用社区阅览室的虚构项目为例，说明「公共利益传播」。

examples.en: Our casebook asks how public-interest communication in the example addresses residents' practical questions about the changed hours.
examples.zh: 案例教材询问，示例中「公共利益传播」怎样回应居民关于时段变动的实际问题。

words.enDefinition: An organised session mainly intended to hear members of the public describe concerns, views, or experiences.

examples.en: At the fictional public listening session, residents describe what they need from a temporary reading facility.
examples.zh: 在虚构「公众意见听取会」上，居民说出他们对临时阅读设施的需求。

examples.en: Our class reads the public listening session summary before considering how the fictional committee responded to common concerns.
examples.zh: 全班阅读「公众意见听取会」摘要，然后考虑虚构委员会如何回应常见关切。

collocations: feedback from a public listening session

words.enDefinition: Journalism using records from public bodies as a substantive source of evidence.

examples.en: The class practiced public records reporting by comparing publicly available versions of the library's annual budget.
examples.zh: 全班比较可公开查阅的各版图书馆年度预算，练习「公共记录报道」。

examples.en: We used public records reporting to follow how the campus shuttle proposal changed before its scheduled review.
examples.zh: 我们用「公共记录报道」方法追踪校园接驳车提案在预定审议前怎样变化。

words.enDefinition: A request to an authority for access to records under an applicable public-access process.

examples.en: The mock public records request asked the library authority for its published budgets and meeting calendars.
examples.zh: 模拟「公开记录申请」请图书馆主管机构提供其发布的预算和会议日程。

examples.en: Our article explained which aggregate spending tables came from a public records request rather than an interview.
examples.zh: 报道说明哪些汇总支出表是经「公开记录申请」取得的，并非采访所得。

collocations: respond to a public records request

words.enDefinition: An official statement that an organisation or representative makes directly available to the public.

examples.en: The fictional library posts a public statement confirming that a temporary reading room is available this week.
examples.zh: 虚构图书馆发布一份「公开声明」，确认本周可以使用一处临时阅览室。

examples.en: Our worksheet compares the public statement with a separate discussion intended only for the fictional organising committee.
examples.zh: 练习单比较「公开声明」与只面向虚构组织委员会的另一项内部讨论。

words.enDefinition: A timetable indicating when an organisation expects to publish new information for the public.

examples.en: The fictional library posts a public update schedule beside its notices about the temporary change to reading rooms.
examples.zh: 虚构图书馆在临时更换阅览室的通知旁公布「公众通报时间表」。

examples.en: Our casebook asks whether the public update schedule was easy to find in the fictional public announcements.
examples.zh: 案例教材询问，在虚构公众公告中，是否很容易找到「公众通报时间表」。

words.enDefinition: An excerpt from an article displayed prominently to catch the reader's attention.

examples.en: The layout editor selected a pull quote from the article to highlight one student's description of the library.
examples.zh: 版面编辑选了文章中一名学生对图书馆的描述，做成一段「突出显示的引文」。

examples.en: We checked that the pull quote matched the article and did not change the speaker's meaning.
examples.zh: 我们核对「突出显示的引文」是否与正文一致，确保没有改变说话者本意。

collocations: display a pull quote alongside the story

words.enDefinition: a scheduling pattern that maintains a low level of advertising with periodic increases in activity

examples.en: The example uses pulsing because the exhibition advertised year-round and added extra spots before school holidays.
examples.zh: 示例属于「脉冲式广告排期」，展览全年有广告，学校放假前还会额外加投。

examples.en: Pulsing let the venue maintain a small weekly presence and increase it before ticket launches.
examples.zh: 「脉冲式广告排期」让场馆每周保持少量曝光，在开票前提高投放量。

words.enDefinition: A factor that makes a consumer less likely or less able to complete a purchase.

examples.en: The class identifies limited storage space as a purchase barrier in the fictional household's product comparison.
examples.zh: 全班将有限的存放空间认定为虚构家庭比较产品时的一项「购买障碍」。

examples.en: Our sample report shows how a purchase barrier affected otherwise interested shoppers in the fictional survey.
examples.zh: 样本报告展示，某项「购买障碍」如何影响虚构调查中原本有兴趣的购物者。

words.enDefinition: The person with the deciding say about whether or what to buy in a shared purchase.

examples.en: The study group identifies the purchase decision maker in the fictional household by reading the dialogue carefully.
examples.zh: 学习小组仔细阅读对话，辨认虚构家庭中的「购买决策者」。

examples.en: Our role map shows the purchase decision maker as one character and the product user as another.
examples.zh: 角色图显示，一名角色是「购买决策者」，另一名角色是产品使用者。

collocations: role of a purchase decision maker
authority of a purchase decision maker

words.enDefinition: The stage in a consumer decision model when the person decides whether, what, or how to buy.

examples.en: Our diagram labels the purchase decision stage after the fictional shopper has compared the remaining products.
examples.zh: 虚构购物者比较完剩余产品后，示意图标出接下来的「购买决策阶段」。

examples.en: The worksheet asks which part of the story belongs to the purchase decision stage in the model.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，故事的哪一部分属于模型中的「购买决策阶段」。

collocations: decisions at the purchase decision stage
factors at the purchase decision stage

words.enDefinition: Postponing a purchase decision while leaving open the possibility of buying later.

examples.en: The fictional diary illustrates purchase deferral when a shopper waits for more information before choosing a lamp.
examples.zh: 虚构日记以购物者等待了解更多信息再挑灯的一幕说明「推迟购买决定」。

examples.en: Our class discusses purchase deferral after reading why the fictional buyer planned to return the following week.
examples.zh: 全班读了虚构买家为什么计划下周再回来，然后讨论「推迟购买决定」。

words.enDefinition: A factor that motivates or strongly influences a consumer's decision to make a purchase.

examples.en: The classroom survey identifies ease of storage as a purchase driver for a fictional group of buyers.
examples.zh: 课堂调查将易于存放列为一个虚构买家群体的「购买驱动因素」。

examples.en: Our summary explains how a purchase driver can differ depending on what students need from the product.
examples.zh: 摘要说明了「购买驱动因素」如何随学生对产品的需求而变化。

words.enDefinition: How often a person or group buys a product or category during a defined period.

examples.en: The fictional report compares purchase frequency across two groups buying sketch paper over the same stated period.
examples.zh: 虚构报告比较两组人在同一指定时段内购买素描纸的「购买频率」。

examples.en: Our worksheet distinguishes purchase frequency from how many items the fictional buyers purchased on each shopping trip.
examples.zh: 练习单把「购买频率」与虚构买家每次购物购买的物品数量分开。

words.enDefinition: Someone whose advice or preferences help shape a purchase decision without necessarily making it.

examples.en: The casebook calls the fictional studio tutor a purchase influencer because their advice shaped the student's choice.
examples.zh: 案例教材将虚构工作室老师称为「购买影响者」，因为老师的意见影响了学生的选择。

examples.en: Our classroom chart separates the purchase influencer from the fictional buyer responsible for paying for the item.
examples.zh: 课堂图表把「购买影响者」与负责付款的虚构买家区分开来。

words.enDefinition: The person who first raises the idea or need for a particular purchase.

examples.en: The fictional household's purchase initiator notices that their shared storage supplies are running low before the discussion.
examples.zh: 虚构家庭的「购买发起者」在讨论前注意到共用收纳用品快用完了。

examples.en: Our role chart lists the purchase initiator separately from the character who will actually buy the item.
examples.zh: 角色表将「购买发起者」与实际购买物品的角色分开列出。

words.enDefinition: A consumer's stated or inferred plan or likelihood of buying a specific product or service.

examples.en: The fictional survey records purchase intention before the students compare it with the later number of actual purchases.
examples.zh: 虚构调查先记录「购买意向」，随后学生将其与后来的实际购买数量对照。

examples.en: Our teacher reminds us that purchase intention can reflect a plan formed before the shopper faces practical constraints.
examples.zh: 老师提醒我们，「购买意向」可能反映购物者遇到实际限制之前所作的计划。

words.enDefinition: The event or situation giving rise to a particular purchase.

examples.en: The example identifies the start of a new art class as the purchase occasion for replacement folders.
examples.zh: 示例将新美术课开课认定为更换文件夹的「购买场合」。

examples.en: Our survey summary distinguishes the purchase occasion from the later situation in which the product was used.
examples.zh: 调查摘要把「购买场合」和后来使用产品的情境区分开来。

words.enDefinition: Disappointment felt after buying, involving the thought that a different choice might have turned out better.

examples.en: The fictional shopper reports purchase regret after thinking that a different notebook might have suited the assignment better.
examples.zh: 虚构购物者觉得另一款笔记本也许更适合这项作业，于是表示有「购后懊悔」。

examples.en: Our seminar distinguishes purchase regret from dissatisfaction that does not involve comparing the choice with an alternative.
examples.zh: 研讨课区分「购后懊悔」和未将所选方案与其他选项作比较时的不满意。

words.enDefinition: In e-commerce, a retailer that sells online and operates no physical stores for customers.

examples.en: The case introduces a pure-play retailer that ships all purchases from its warehouse.
examples.zh: 案例介绍了一家所有商品都从仓库发出的「纯线上零售商」。

examples.en: We compared the pure-play retailer with a seller that also operated neighborhood stores.
examples.zh: 我们将「纯线上零售商」与同时经营社区门店的卖家作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Systematic review of delivery material for technical problems against specified requirements

examples.en: The quality-control pass flags a subtitle that remains visible beyond the final shot.
examples.zh: 「一轮技术质检」发现有一条字幕在最后一个镜头结束后仍显示。

examples.en: We scheduled a quality-control pass after exporting the file for our mock broadcaster.
examples.zh: 我们为模拟播出机构导出文件后安排了「一轮技术质检」。

words.enDefinition: Checking a quotation for accuracy against an interview, notes, or other reliable record.

examples.en: The editor completed quote verification by comparing the sentence with the recorded interview and the reporter's notes.
examples.zh: 编辑把句子和采访录音、记者笔记比对，完成了「引语核对」。

examples.en: We used quote verification to check the speaker's wording before fitting the sentence into the report.
examples.zh: 我们在把句子写进报道前，通过「引语核对」确认说话者的原话。

words.enDefinition: Wholesaler supplying products and managing their display racks inside retail stores

examples.en: The class example uses a rack jobber to restock and manage a greeting-card rack.
examples.zh: 课堂示例使用「货架代营批发商」补货并管理贺卡陈列架。

examples.en: We checked who maintained the shelf before identifying the rack jobber in the scenario.
examples.zh: 我们先查看谁维护货架，再辨认出情境里的「货架代营批发商」。

collocations: displays managed by a rack jobber

words.enDefinition: An innovation representing a substantial departure from previous products, technologies, or practices.

examples.en: The example counted as radical innovation because the offering met the need in a fundamentally different way.
examples.zh: 这个例子属于「突破式创新」，因为所提供的产品或服务以根本不同的方式满足需求。

examples.en: We debated whether the redesign qualified as radical innovation or simply improved a familiar product concept.
examples.zh: 我们讨论，这次重新设计属于「突破式创新」，还是只是改进了熟悉的产品概念。

collocations: radical innovation in a product category

words.enDefinition: a persuasive approach based on reasons, facts, or practical product benefits

examples.en: The poster used a rational appeal by showing the yearly repair costs for both options.
examples.zh: 海报展现两种方案的年度维修费用，采用了「理性诉求」。

examples.en: The class identified a rational appeal in the brochure's comparison of energy use and purchase price.
examples.zh: 全班在宣传册对能耗和购买价格的比较中辨认出「理性诉求」。

words.enDefinition: Post-production specialist combining dialogue, music, and effects into the final mix

examples.en: The re-recording mixer balances the music with the actors' dialogue in the scene.
examples.zh: 「后期混音师」平衡了该场戏中音乐与演员对白的音量。

examples.en: We asked the re-recording mixer to review two versions of the closing sequence.
examples.zh: 我们请「后期混音师」检查收尾段落的两个版本。

words.enDefinition: A statement prepared or issued in response to an external question or a new development.

examples.en: The fictional press office issues a reactive statement after a journalist asks about the missing exhibition dates.
examples.zh: 在记者询问未列明的展出日期后，虚构新闻联络办公室发出一份「应询声明」。

examples.en: Our case compares the reactive statement with an announcement the fictional gallery already planned to publish later.
examples.zh: 案例把「应询声明」与虚构画廊已计划稍后公布的公告作比较。

words.enDefinition: evidence or a concrete product feature that supports an advertised promise

examples.en: In the brief, a longer tested battery life was the reason to believe the promise of fewer interruptions.
examples.zh: 在简报里，实测续航更长是「可信依据」，支撑了使用中断更少的承诺。

examples.en: The writers added a reason to believe by citing the published results from the materials test.
examples.zh: 文案人员引用公开的材料测试结果，为主张补上了「可信依据」。

collocations: include a reason to believe in the brief

words.enDefinition: A substantial change to an established brand's name, identity, or public presentation.

examples.en: The fictional store considered rebranding after deciding its old name no longer represented the wider product selection.
examples.zh: 虚构商店认为旧名称已不能代表其更丰富的产品，于是考虑「品牌重塑」。

examples.en: We compared a limited design update with rebranding that would replace the shop's existing name entirely.
examples.zh: 我们将有限的设计更新与彻底替换原店名的「品牌重塑」作比较。

words.enDefinition: Documentation showing the fields, order, and structure of records in a source dataset.

examples.en: The record layout identified the column containing visit dates before the team started reading the table.
examples.zh: 小组开始读表之前，「数据记录字段布局」标出了存放到访日期的那一列。

examples.en: We reviewed the record layout to see whether the file distinguished new loans from renewals.
examples.zh: 我们审阅「数据记录字段布局」，看文件是否区分首次借阅和续借。

collocations: compare a file with its record layout

words.enDefinition: Document specifying the order in which parties recover amounts from receipts

examples.en: The recoupment schedule shows which costs are recovered before other participants receive payments.
examples.zh: 「回款分配顺序表」说明了哪些成本先收回，之后其他参与方才获得款项。

examples.en: We traced a sample payment through the recoupment schedule in the finance exercise.
examples.zh: 融资练习中，我们沿着「回款分配顺序表」追踪了一笔样例款项。

words.enDefinition: A group a consumer uses as a point of comparison or as a source of norms or information.

examples.en: The fictional shopper treats a campus art club as a reference group when considering supplies for workshops.
examples.zh: 虚构购物者在考虑工作坊用品时，把校园美术社视为「参照群体」。

examples.en: Our seminar asks which reference group provides a point of comparison in the imaginary buyer's account.
examples.zh: 研讨课询问，虚构买家的记述中哪一个「参照群体」提供了比较依据。

collocations: use a reference group for comparison

words.enDefinition: Emergence or addition of intermediaries after a distribution route becomes more direct

examples.en: The case shows reintermediation when a new marketplace links makers and buyers again.
examples.zh: 案例中，新的交易平台重新连接生产商和买家，表现出「再中介化」。

examples.en: The case illustrated reintermediation when a booking platform took over sales previously handled directly by the venues.
examples.zh: 一家订票平台接手原由场馆直接完成的销售，案例用这一变化说明「再中介化」。

words.enDefinition: The perceived improvement an innovation offers over the approach it replaces.

examples.en: Easy refilling gave the new notebook a relative advantage over the older model in the classroom case.
examples.zh: 课堂案例中，补充纸页更方便，使新笔记本比旧款具有「创新的相对优势」。

examples.en: We discussed whether the fictional buyers perceived enough relative advantage to switch from the tool they already used.
examples.zh: 我们讨论虚构买家是否察觉到足够的「创新的相对优势」，从而愿意换掉正在用的工具。

words.enDefinition: Specified period during which a title is available through a distribution outlet

examples.en: The case assigns one release window to the cinema and another to streaming.
examples.zh: 案例为影院和流媒体分别安排了一个「发行窗口期」。

examples.en: We compared the dates for each release window on the fictional launch calendar.
examples.zh: 我们比较了虚构发行日历中各个「发行窗口期」的日期。

words.enDefinition: advertising that keeps an established offering or recurring occasion in the audience's mind

examples.en: The shop used reminder advertising each spring to bring its annual bike service to mind.
examples.zh: 商店每年春天用「提醒性广告」让顾客想起年度自行车保养服务。

examples.en: The festival scheduled reminder advertising a week before its established summer opening date.
examples.zh: 电影节在历年的夏季开幕日期前一周安排了「提醒性广告」。

collocations: reminder advertising for an established brand

words.enDefinition: advertising space, time, or impressions left unsold after primary sales commitments

examples.en: The station offered remnant inventory when its regular buyers had finished booking weekend airtime.
examples.zh: 常规客户预订完周末播出时段后，电台推出了「剩余广告库存」。

examples.en: Our worksheet compared the quoted rate for remnant inventory with the price of guaranteed placements.
examples.zh: 练习单把「剩余广告库存」的报价与有保证的投放价格作了对比。

words.enDefinition: Restating what someone said without presenting it as their exact words.

examples.en: The reader could tell from the reported speech that the writer was summarizing the organizer's explanation.
examples.zh: 读者从「间接引语」看出，作者是在概述组织人员的解释。

examples.en: We used reported speech for the routine details and reserved quotation marks for the librarian's exact words.
examples.zh: 我们用「间接引语」转述常规细节，只给图书管理员的原话加引号。

collocations: convert a quotation into reported speech
distinguish reported speech from direct quotation

words.enDefinition: The stated or inferred likelihood that someone with prior purchase experience will buy the offering again.

examples.en: The fictional survey measures repurchase intention among participants who previously bought an item for the studio.
examples.zh: 虚构调查在以前为工作室购买过该物品的参与者中测量「再次购买意向」。

examples.en: Our class contrasts repurchase intention with a recorded second purchase in the fictional research results table.
examples.zh: 全班将「再次购买意向」与虚构研究结果表中记录的第二次购买作比较。

words.enDefinition: A journalist's invitation for a story subject to address specific claims or questions before publication.

examples.en: The reporter sent a request for comment outlining the questions about the library's revised timetable.
examples.zh: 记者发出了「征询置评请求」，列明有关图书馆调整时间表的问题。

examples.en: The draft noted when the request for comment was sent and whether an answer had arrived.
examples.zh: 草稿注明何时发出「征询置评请求」，以及是否已经收到答复。

collocations: respond to a request for comment

words.enDefinition: A person or organisation that requests and usually funds a study carried out by a research provider.

examples.en: The role chart identifies the research commissioner as the fictional organisation asking for the market study.
examples.zh: 角色图将要求进行市场研究的虚构机构列为「调研委托方」。

examples.en: Our class asks how the research commissioner expressed the decision context in the fictional briefing document.
examples.zh: 全班询问，「调研委托方」在虚构任务说明中怎样表述决策背景。

words.enDefinition: The number or set of respondents whose answers are included in a reported survey calculation.

examples.en: The fictional chart specifies the respondent base below each percentage to show who is included in the calculation.
examples.zh: 虚构图在各百分比下方注明「受访者计算基数」，说明计算时涉及哪些人。

examples.en: Our worksheet shows that the respondent base changes when only fictional users answer the question about product use.
examples.zh: 练习单显示，只让虚构用户回答产品使用问题时，「受访者计算基数」会变化。

collocations: percentage calculated on a respondent base

words.zhGloss: 对公众意见征询的正式回应
words.enDefinition: An organisation's public account of how it considered feedback from a consultation and what it proposes to do next.
acceptedZhAnswers: 对公众意见征询的正式回应

examples.en: The fictional university's response to public consultation explains why one option changed after comments from library users.
examples.zh: 虚构大学的「对公众意见征询的正式回应」解释，为什么收到图书馆使用者意见后修改了一项选项。

examples.en: Our class compares the response to public consultation with the document that originally invited feedback in the exercise.
examples.zh: 全班将「对公众意见征询的正式回应」与练习中最初征询意见的文件作比较。

collocations: publish a response to public consultation
draft a response to public consultation
decision explained in a response to public consultation

words.enDefinition: Retail business operating multiple stores under common control or branding

examples.en: The retail chain in our case uses the same name at every location.
examples.zh: 案例中的「连锁零售企业」在所有地点使用相同的名称。

examples.en: We compared one retail chain location with an independently operated shop nearby.
examples.zh: 我们将「连锁零售企业」的一家门店与附近一家独立经营的店作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Type of retail operation defined by its assortment, service, and selling method

examples.en: The class compares a membership warehouse with another retail format offering personal assistance.
examples.zh: 课堂对比了会员仓储店与另一种提供专人协助的「零售业态」。

examples.en: We identified the retail format by looking at the seller's assortment and service model.
examples.zh: 我们通过查看卖家的商品组合和服务模式来辨认「零售业态」。

words.enDefinition: Reduction of an item's current retail selling price from its earlier level

examples.en: The store in the example records a retail markdown on its remaining seasonal stock.
examples.zh: 示例中的商店对剩余的季节性库存记录了一次「零售价下调」。

examples.en: We compared the original and revised prices to calculate the retail markdown.
examples.zh: 我们对照原价和调整后的价格，计算「零售价下调」幅度。

words.enDefinition: A public statement withdrawing previously published material and explaining that it should no longer be relied on.

examples.en: The fictional paper posted a retraction notice when the central claim of the article proved unsupported.
examples.zh: 文章的核心说法经查缺少依据时，虚构报纸发布了「撤稿声明」。

examples.en: We compared a retraction notice with a correction that left the rest of the student story unchanged.
examples.zh: 我们把「撤稿声明」与学生报道中只修改一处、其余内容仍保留的更正作比较。

words.enDefinition: revenue attributed to advertising divided by the amount spent on that advertising

examples.en: The retailer calculated return on ad spend using sales revenue attributed to the spring campaign.
examples.zh: 零售商用归因于春季宣传的销售收入计算「广告支出回报率」。

examples.en: Our class recalculated return on ad spend after finding that the table omitted one media charge.
examples.zh: 课堂发现表中漏了一笔媒体费用，因此重新计算了「广告支出回报率」。

collocations: return on ad spend by campaign

words.enDefinition: Combining returned products into fewer shipments before moving them onward

examples.en: The case illustrates returns consolidation when several stores send returns together for inspection.
examples.zh: 案例用几家门店把退货合在一起送检的情形说明「退货集运」。

examples.en: We compared returns consolidation with sending each returned item directly to the supplier.
examples.zh: 我们将「退货集运」与每件退货都直接寄给供应商的做法作了比较。

words.enDefinition: A search using an image to find matching or visually similar images already available.

examples.en: The class used reverse image search to see whether the public campus photograph had appeared before.
examples.zh: 全班用「以图搜图」检查这张公开校园照片以前是否出现过。

examples.en: A reverse image search found the same photograph in an older public brochure for the exhibition.
examples.zh: 通过「以图搜图」，我们在一份较早的公开展览手册中找到了同一张照片。

collocations: results from a reverse image search
a reverse image search for a picture

words.enDefinition: Movement of products back through the supply chain for recovery or disposition

examples.en: The chart uses reverse logistics to trace returned items from stores back to warehouses.
examples.zh: 图表通过「逆向物流」追踪退回商品从门店回到仓库的过程。

examples.en: We discussed reverse logistics when the mock retailer sent returned goods for inspection.
examples.zh: 模拟零售商将退货送检时，我们讨论了「逆向物流」。

words.enDefinition: The opportunity for a person or organization criticized in a report to respond to the relevant claims.

examples.en: Before publication, the editor offered a right of reply to the people criticized in the fictional article.
examples.zh: 刊发前，编辑给虚构报道中受到批评的人提供了「回应权」。

examples.en: Our class discussed whether the right of reply gave the organization enough time to address the concerns.
examples.zh: 全班讨论，报道是否为有关机构充分行使「回应权」留出了时间。

collocations: an opportunity under a right of reply

words.enDefinition: Return of previously granted rights to the original holder under stated conditions

examples.en: The mock deal includes rights reversion after the agreed license period ends.
examples.zh: 模拟协议规定，约定的许可期结束后发生「权利回归」。

examples.en: We identified which party received the rights again under the rights reversion clause.
examples.zh: 我们辨认出根据「权利回归」条款，权利重新归到哪一方。

words.enDefinition: Ambient sound recorded in a location without deliberate speech or action

examples.en: The sound crew records room tone after the actors finish the reading room scene.
examples.zh: 演员拍完阅览室场景后，录音组录下了「室内环境底声」。

examples.en: We used room tone to smooth the transition between two lines of dialogue.
examples.zh: 我们用「室内环境底声」让两句对白之间的过渡更自然。

words.enDefinition: Early edited version showing the developing structure before detailed refinement

examples.en: The rough cut gives our classmates enough material to comment on the story.
examples.zh: 「粗剪版」的内容已经足够让同学对故事提出意见。

examples.en: We compared the rough cut with the revised version after making the suggested changes.
examples.zh: 按照建议修改后，我们对比了「粗剪版」和修改后的版本。

words.enDefinition: Communication giving verified information to correct an unconfirmed claim circulating among the public or within a group.

examples.en: The fictional library's rumour correction confirms that the temporary reading room remains open on its usual days.
examples.zh: 虚构图书馆的「传言纠正」确认，临时阅览室仍按通常日期开放。

examples.en: Our exercise checks whether the rumour correction cites the confirmed schedule for the fictional public reading programme.
examples.zh: 练习核对「传言纠正」是否引用了虚构公共阅读项目已经确认的日程。

collocations: verified information in a rumour correction

words.enDefinition: Recently recorded footage prepared for review during or shortly after filming

examples.en: The editor reviews the rushes before assembling the scene for the tutorial.
examples.zh: 剪辑师先查看「当日拍摄素材」，再为辅导课把场景剪接起来。

examples.en: We noticed a change in lighting while comparing two takes from the rushes.
examples.zh: 我们对照两条「当日拍摄素材」时注意到光线变了。

words.enDefinition: Setting prices primarily to increase sales volume or market share

examples.en: The case models sales-oriented pricing by giving sales volume priority over immediate profit.
examples.zh: 案例将销量置于眼前利润之上，以示范「销量导向定价」。

examples.en: We identified sales-oriented pricing after checking which outcome the classroom model emphasized.
examples.zh: 我们查看课堂模型着重追求哪项结果后，识别出了「销量导向定价」。

words.enDefinition: Retail sales divided by the relevant floor area measured in square feet

examples.en: The workbook compares sales per square foot for two layouts with different amounts of selling space.
examples.zh: 练习册比较了销售面积不同的两种布局的「每平方英尺销售额」。

examples.en: Our project uses sales per square foot to examine how much revenue each layout generates.
examples.zh: 我们用「每平方英尺销售额」考察各种布局的创收表现。

words.enDefinition: Sales from a comparable group of stores operating in both reporting periods

examples.en: The sample report separates same-store sales from revenue at the newly opened locations.
examples.zh: 示例报告把「可比门店销售额」与新开门店的收入分开列出。

examples.en: We used same-store sales to compare the established stores across two fictional years.
examples.zh: 我们用「可比门店销售额」比较两个虚构年度里既有门店的表现。

words.enDefinition: Rights to adapt an existing work for a film or television production

examples.en: The fictional producer seeks screen rights to adapt the novel for television.
examples.zh: 虚构制片人想取得「影视改编权」，把小说改编成电视剧。

examples.en: We checked who held screen rights in the sample project rights summary.
examples.zh: 我们在项目权利摘要的示例中确认了谁持有「影视改编权」。

words.enDefinition: Prose account outlining a proposed film's story, main characters, and progression

examples.en: The screenplay treatment summarizes the main scenes before the writers draft the dialogue.
examples.zh: 编剧起草对白前，先用「剧本故事梗概」概述主要场景。

examples.en: We read the screenplay treatment to see how the two plotlines would connect.
examples.zh: 我们阅读「剧本故事梗概」，查看两条情节线会如何衔接。

words.enDefinition: Scene-by-scene inventory of cast, locations, props, and other requirements for filming

examples.en: The script breakdown lists performers, locations, and props for each scene in the film.
examples.zh: 「剧本拆解清单」列出了影片每场戏的演员、场地和道具。

examples.en: We used the script breakdown to identify scenes that shared a filming location.
examples.zh: 我们用「剧本拆解清单」找出共用同一拍摄地点的几场戏。

words.enDefinition: Reader's written summary and evaluation of a screenplay for development decisions

examples.en: Our tutor assigned script coverage for a sample screenplay about two student musicians.
examples.zh: 老师布置我们为一部关于两名学生乐手的示例剧本撰写「剧本评估报告」。

examples.en: We compared the script coverage with the script to see which concerns it emphasized.
examples.zh: 我们将「剧本评估报告」与剧本对照，查看它重点指出了哪些问题。

words.enDefinition: Development professional who works with writers to improve scripts and maintain coherence

examples.en: The script editor flags a scene that conflicts with an earlier draft decision.
examples.zh: 「剧本编辑」指出一场戏与前一稿确立的情节有冲突。

examples.en: We discussed the script editor notes before rewriting the ending of our scene.
examples.zh: 我们先讨论了「剧本编辑」的意见，再改写那场戏的结尾。

words.enDefinition: Replacement pages documenting changes to a script during an active production

examples.en: The coordinator distributes script revision pages after the location change affects the evening scene.
examples.zh: 拍摄地点变更影响晚间场次后，协调员发放了「剧本修订页」。

examples.en: We checked the date on the script revision pages before updating our scene notes.
examples.zh: 更新场次笔记之前，我们核对了「剧本修订页」上的日期。

words.enDefinition: On-set crew member tracking continuity, takes, and changes for the edit

examples.en: The script supervisor records which version of the line appears in each take.
examples.zh: 「影视场记」记录每条素材中说的是哪个版本的台词。

examples.en: We checked with the script supervisor before repeating the action from another angle.
examples.zh: 我们先和「影视场记」核对，再换一个角度重演该动作。

words.enDefinition: paid placement of advertisements on search results pages in response to related queries

examples.en: The repair shop used search advertising to appear alongside relevant searches about repairing lamps.
examples.zh: 维修店用「搜索广告」在修灯相关的搜索结果旁展示广告。

examples.en: In the assignment, students compared search advertising with print placements for the same repair service.
examples.zh: 作业中，学生比较了同一维修服务的「搜索广告」和平面广告版位。

words.enDefinition: Price reduction offered for purchases made during a designated seasonal period

examples.en: The workbook describes a seasonal discount for retailers ordering display fixtures outside peak season.
examples.zh: 练习册描述了零售商在销售淡季订购展示设备时获得的「季节折扣」。

examples.en: We checked when buyers qualified for the seasonal discount in the example.
examples.zh: 我们查看了示例中买家什么时候能享受「季节折扣」。

words.enDefinition: Separate crew filming assigned material alongside or apart from the main unit

examples.en: The second unit films exterior details while the main crew works indoors.
examples.zh: 主要摄制组在室内工作时，「第二摄制组」负责拍外景细节。

examples.en: We checked which landscape shots were assigned to the second unit in the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们核对了练习中哪些风景镜头分给了「第二摄制组」。

collocations: assign shots to the second unit

words.enDefinition: Packaging that groups or protects one or more already packaged units.

examples.en: The box holding several individually wrapped tea sachets served as secondary packaging in the case.
examples.zh: 案例中，装着多袋独立包装茶叶的盒子充当「外层包装」。

examples.en: We compared secondary packaging that grouped the same units in two differently shaped display boxes.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两类「外层包装」，它们用形状不同的展示盒装相同的独立包装产品。

words.enDefinition: A description based on information received from someone else rather than from direct experience.

examples.en: The reporter treated the message as a secondhand account because its writer had not attended the workshop.
examples.zh: 消息的撰写者没有参加工作坊，记者将它当作「转述所得的陈述」。

examples.en: We checked the secondhand account against a public record before including it in the campus article.
examples.zh: 在校园报道中采用这份「转述所得的陈述」之前，我们用公开记录作了核对。

collocations: compare a secondhand account with direct evidence

words.enDefinition: The extent to which a business can reach and serve members of a market segment under stated conditions.

examples.en: The seminar assesses segment accessibility using the delivery areas described in a fictional supplier's public service summary.
examples.zh: 研讨课依据虚构供应商公开服务摘要中描述的配送地区评估「细分群体可触达性」。

examples.en: Our class discusses segment accessibility separately from the potential size of the audience in the fictional market.
examples.zh: 全班将「细分群体可触达性」与虚构市场中的潜在受众规模分开讨论。

words.enDefinition: The extent to which available resources and capabilities can support practical offerings or plans for a segment.

examples.en: The case discusses segment actionability by comparing the imagined supplier's capabilities with the stated needs of the group.
examples.zh: 案例将想象中供应商的能力与群体所述需求对照，用来讨论「细分群体可实施性」。

examples.en: Our seminar examines why segment actionability may differ even between two similarly sized fictional groups of consumers.
examples.zh: 研讨课探讨，即使两个虚构消费者群体规模相近，「细分群体可实施性」为何也可能不同。

words.enDefinition: The extent to which a market segment can be meaningfully distinguished from others in relevant needs or responses.

examples.en: The fictional report illustrates segment differentiability by comparing groups whose members value different outcomes from the same product.
examples.zh: 虚构报告比较重视同一产品不同使用结果的群体，说明「细分群体可区分性」。

examples.en: Our class compares reactions across the fictional groups to see whether there is evidence of segment differentiability.
examples.zh: 全班比较虚构群体之间的反应，看看能否找到有关「细分群体可区分性」的证据。

words.enDefinition: The possibility that a market segment will grow in size, demand, or economic value over time.

examples.en: Our casebook compares segment growth potential using two alternative sets of assumptions about the fictional market outlook.
examples.zh: 案例教材采用两套关于虚构市场前景的假设来比较「细分群体增长潜力」。

examples.en: The classroom report discusses segment growth potential separately from the current size of the fictional buyer population.
examples.zh: 课堂报告将「细分群体增长潜力」与虚构买家总体的当前规模分开讨论。

words.enDefinition: The extent to which a segment's size and relevant characteristics can be estimated with available evidence.

examples.en: The textbook illustrates segment measurability by comparing classes with published aggregate counts and classes without adequate counts.
examples.zh: 教材比较有已公布汇总人数的类别和缺乏足够统计的类别，用来说明「细分群体可衡量性」。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks which part of the fictional summary provides evidence about segment measurability in the example.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，虚构摘要的哪一部分为示例中的「细分群体可衡量性」提供依据。

words.enDefinition: A situation where two market segments share some members or features under the criteria used.

examples.en: The example shows segment overlap when some fictional respondents meet the criteria for two groups in the table.
examples.zh: 示例显示，部分虚构应答者同时符合表中两个群体的标准，因而出现「细分群体重叠」。

examples.en: Our class notes segment overlap before combining the counts listed for the fictional project in two categories.
examples.zh: 全班先留意「细分群体重叠」，再合并虚构项目归入两个类别的人数。

words.enDefinition: A description of a market segment's relevant characteristics, needs, and typical buying or use patterns.

examples.en: The students read a segment profile summarising preferences across a fictional group of buyers in the exercise.
examples.zh: 学生阅读了一个「细分群体概貌」，其中概括了练习里一个虚构买家群体的偏好。

examples.en: Our class compares two versions of a segment profile based on different summaries of the same fictional survey.
examples.zh: 全班比较了基于同一虚构调查的不同摘要写成的两份「细分群体概貌」。

words.enDefinition: The extent to which serving a segment can generate profit under specified revenue, cost, and other assumptions.

examples.en: The fictional report discusses segment profitability by presenting estimated revenue and estimated costs in adjacent table columns.
examples.zh: 虚构报告相邻两列分别给出预计收入和预计成本，用以讨论「细分群体盈利性」。

examples.en: Our seminar separates segment profitability from the larger number of customers described in one of the fictional profiles.
examples.zh: 研讨课把「细分群体盈利性」与虚构画像之一所描述的较大客户人数分开。

words.enDefinition: The estimated count or proportion of consumers belonging to a market segment.

examples.en: The fictional market report gives segment size as both a count and a percentage of all buyers.
examples.zh: 虚构市场报告用人数和占所有买家的百分比两种方式表示「细分群体规模」。

examples.en: Our class compares segment size across two estimates that use different reference populations for the fictional example.
examples.zh: 全班比较虚构示例中使用不同基准总体的两个估计所给出的「细分群体规模」。

words.enDefinition: The degree to which a segment is sufficiently large or valuable to justify serving it under stated conditions.

examples.en: The class discusses segment substantiality by comparing the fictional groups with the costs described in the example.
examples.zh: 全班把示例描述的成本与虚构群体对照，用来讨论「细分群体规模充足性」。

examples.en: Our worksheet distinguishes segment substantiality from the practical ability to deliver the offering to the fictional users.
examples.zh: 练习单将「细分群体规模充足性」与实际能否向虚构用户交付产品分开。

words.enDefinition: A characteristic, kind of information, or criterion used to divide a market into distinct groups.

examples.en: The fictional study uses intended use as its segmentation base for grouping buyers of art supplies.
examples.zh: 虚构研究根据预定用途对美术用品买家分组，把它作为「市场细分依据」。

examples.en: Our seminar asks why the same market might yield different groups under a different segmentation base.
examples.zh: 研讨课询问，同一个市场按照不同的「市场细分依据」为什么会形成不同的群体。

collocations: compare a segmentation base with another

words.enDefinition: Distribution of an offering through a chosen subset of available outlets

examples.en: The appliance case uses selective distribution and chooses outlets that can explain the product.
examples.zh: 家电案例采用「选择性分销」，挑选能够讲解产品的网点。

examples.en: We discussed selective distribution after comparing retailer service in the class handout.
examples.zh: 我们比较了课堂讲义中的零售服务之后，讨论了「选择性分销」。

words.enDefinition: A way an offering helps customers express their identity or values.

examples.en: The self-expressive benefit of the interchangeable covers was that students could show their own design preferences.
examples.zh: 可替换封皮带来的「自我表达利益」是让学生能展现自己的设计偏好。

examples.en: We compared the self-expressive benefit of visible club badges with the practical benefit of a stronger bag.
examples.zh: 我们比较了显眼的社团徽章带来的「自我表达利益」与包袋更加结实带来的实际好处。

words.enDefinition: Making the distinction between reported news and advocacy or personal opinion clear to readers.

examples.en: The redesigned labels made the separation of news and opinion clear on the newspaper's homepage.
examples.zh: 重新设计的栏目标签让读者一眼就能看出，报纸首页遵循「新闻与评论分开」的原则。

examples.en: Our class examined the separation of news and opinion by comparing an article with its accompanying column.
examples.zh: 全班把报道与配发的专栏作比较，考察「新闻与评论分开」在样刊中的做法。

collocations: maintain separation of news and opinion
a policy on separation of news and opinion
reinforce separation of news and opinion

words.enDefinition: A test in which a participant evaluates several concepts or products one at a time, rating each separately.

examples.en: The classroom summary describes a sequential monadic test with separate ratings of each fictional product idea in order.
examples.zh: 课堂摘要描述了一项「顺序独立测评」，按次序分别给每个虚构产品构想评分。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks whether earlier items might affect scores later in a fictional sequential monadic test report.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，在虚构「顺序独立测评」报告中，先出现的项目是否可能影响后面的评分。

collocations: results of a sequential monadic test
order effects in a sequential monadic test

words.enDefinition: Reference document describing a series' world, characters, and approach across episodes

examples.en: The writers consult the series bible when outlining a story for another episode.
examples.zh: 编剧构思另一集的故事时，查阅了「剧集设定手册」。

examples.en: Our group included episode ideas and recurring settings in the series bible.
examples.zh: 我们组把每集的构思和反复出现的场景写进了「剧集设定手册」。

words.enDefinition: Commission authorizing production of a specified run of episodes for a series

examples.en: The fictional broadcaster issues a series order after the commissioner reviews a sample episode.
examples.zh: 虚构播出机构的委制负责人看完样片后，机构发出了「剧集制作订单」。

examples.en: We noted how many episodes the series order covered in the fictional memo.
examples.zh: 我们记下了虚构备忘录中的「剧集制作订单」包含多少集。

words.enDefinition: A brand identifying an ongoing service or a provider's service experience.

examples.en: Our case gave the bicycle lending program a service brand that appeared on signs and reservation screens.
examples.zh: 我们的案例为自行车借用计划设定了一个「服务品牌」，用在标牌和预约界面上。

examples.en: We discussed how the service brand helped students recognize the fictional tutoring service across different locations.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「服务品牌」如何帮助学生在不同地点认出该虚构辅导服务。

words.enDefinition: A public notice explaining a temporary interruption or change to a service and, where known, its expected scope.

examples.en: The fictional college posts a service disruption notice after the main study room becomes temporarily unavailable.
examples.zh: 主要自习室暂时无法使用后，虚构大学张贴了「服务中断通知」。

examples.en: Our worksheet checks which temporary arrangements are described in the service disruption notice for the fictional library.
examples.zh: 练习单核对虚构图书馆的「服务中断通知」说明了哪些临时安排。

collocations: details in a service disruption notice

words.enDefinition: Reporting that gives readers practical information they can use in everyday decisions.

examples.en: The transport guide was service journalism because readers could use it to choose a campus bus route.
examples.zh: 交通指南属于「实用服务新闻」，读者可以据此选择校园公交线路。

examples.en: The class discussed service journalism after comparing two guides to using the library's public study rooms.
examples.zh: 全班比较两份图书馆公共自习室使用指南后，讨论了「实用服务新闻」。

words.enDefinition: A notice describing when or to what extent an interrupted service has become available again.

examples.en: The fictional museum issues a service restoration update confirming that the public reading room has reopened today.
examples.zh: 虚构博物馆发布一则「服务恢复通报」，确认公共阅览室今天已重新开放。

examples.en: Our class compares the service restoration update with the earlier notice listing temporary alternatives at the library.
examples.zh: 全班把「服务恢复通报」与此前列明图书馆临时替代方案的通知作比较。

collocations: timing in a service restoration update

words.enDefinition: Crew member overseeing furnishings and decorative objects that dress a set

examples.en: The set decorator selects chairs and lamps for the fictional reading room.
examples.zh: 「布景陈设师」为虚构阅览室挑选椅子和灯具。

examples.en: We showed the set decorator the reference photographs for our student set.
examples.zh: 我们给「布景陈设师」看了学生剧组布景的参考照片。

words.enDefinition: a brand's advertising expenditure as a proportion of the expenditure measured for a category or market

examples.en: The chart compares share of spend for three footwear brands in the same advertising market.
examples.zh: 图表比较同一广告市场里三个鞋类品牌的「广告支出份额」。

examples.en: The analyst calculated share of spend using the reported media costs for every brand in the category.
examples.zh: 分析人员根据该品类所有品牌申报的媒体费用，计算「广告支出份额」。

words.enDefinition: a brand's proportion of the measured promotional exposure or mentions within a market category

examples.en: The analyst estimated share of voice using the brands' total impressions across the same four publications.
examples.zh: 分析人员用各品牌在同样四种刊物上的展示量估算「广告声量份额」。

examples.en: Two brands spent similar amounts but had different share of voice when the class counted impressions.
examples.zh: 课堂按展示次数计算时，两品牌花费相近，「广告声量份额」却不同。

words.enDefinition: In the PESO model, communication shared or co-created by organisations and audiences on social platforms or similar networks.

examples.en: The classroom example illustrates shared media through a fictional community group's voluntary repost of a university announcement.
examples.zh: 课堂示例借虚构社区团体自愿转发大学公告的一幕说明「社交共创传播」。

examples.en: The team credited shared media when local readers discussed and recirculated the library's opening announcement.
examples.zh: 本地读者讨论并转发图书馆开放公告时，团队把这种传播视为「社交共创传播」。

words.enDefinition: Number of visible front-facing units allocated to a product on shelves

examples.en: The class compares shelf facings for two items sharing the same shelf.
examples.zh: 课堂比较了共用同一货架的两款商品的「货架陈列面数」。

examples.en: We counted the shelf facings from the aisle, excluding stock behind the front row.
examples.zh: 我们站在通道里数「货架陈列面数」，未把后排库存算进去。

words.enDefinition: Fulfillment option in which a retail store ships orders from its inventory

examples.en: The fictional retailer offers ship from store when its warehouse runs out of a product.
examples.zh: 虚构零售商的仓库缺某款商品时，会提供「门店发货」。

examples.en: We compared ship from store with shipping the same online order from a central warehouse.
examples.zh: 我们将「门店发货」与由中央仓库发出同一线上订单的做法作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Fulfillment option sending an order to a store for customer collection

examples.en: The case offers ship-to-store when the pickup store lacks the ordered item.
examples.zh: 如果取货门店没有所订商品，案例就提供「发往门店自提」。

examples.en: We distinguished ship-to-store from reserving an item already on the store shelf.
examples.zh: 我们区分了「发往门店自提」与预留门店货架上已有的商品。

words.enDefinition: Production-ready screenplay formatted as a working reference for filming

examples.en: The shooting script uses stable scene numbers so different departments can coordinate.
examples.zh: 「拍摄剧本」采用固定的场次编号，方便不同部门协调工作。

examples.en: We checked the shooting script after the location change affected two planned scenes.
examples.zh: 更换地点影响原定两场戏之后，我们查阅了「拍摄剧本」。

words.enDefinition: An offering buyers typically compare on suitability, quality, style, or price before choosing.

examples.en: Our classroom case classified a desk chair as a shopping product because students compared several models.
examples.zh: 在我们的课堂案例中，学生比较多个型号后才决定，因此书桌椅被归为「选购品」。

examples.en: The fictional buyers chose a shopping product after checking how well each model fitted their workspace.
examples.zh: 虚构买家核对各型号与学习空间的适配程度，才选定这种「选购品」。

collocations: classify an item as a shopping product

words.enDefinition: Variety of shots recorded to provide editing choices for a scene

examples.en: The director reviews shot coverage before leaving the location used for the conversation.
examples.zh: 导演在离开对话场景的拍摄地之前查看了「场景镜头覆盖」情况。

examples.en: We compared the planned shot coverage with the angles available in the edit.
examples.zh: 我们将计划中的「场景镜头覆盖」与剪辑时实际可用的角度作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Examining an item in a physical store before purchasing it online

examples.en: The case describes showrooming when a shopper tries the item before ordering online.
examples.zh: 案例描述购物者先到店试用再上网下单的「先看店后网购」行为。

examples.en: We mapped showrooming as a journey beginning in the physical shop.
examples.zh: 我们把「先看店后网购」画成一条从实体店开始的购物路径。

words.enDefinition: Writer-producer overseeing a series' creative direction and day-to-day production decisions

examples.en: The showrunner in the mock production balances writing deadlines and filming needs.
examples.zh: 模拟制作中的「剧集总负责人」协调编剧期限与拍摄需求。

examples.en: Our tutor explained why the showrunner approves changes that affect several episodes.
examples.zh: 老师解释了为什么会影响多集的改动要由「剧集总负责人」批准。

words.enDefinition: A companion news piece presenting a focused aspect of a larger main report.

examples.en: The sidebar story explained the free shuttle route that the main article could only mention briefly.
examples.zh: 「主稿配发短文」详细介绍了主稿只能简短提及的免费接驳车路线。

examples.en: Our editor assigned a sidebar story about the timetable and saved the policy debate for the main report.
examples.zh: 编辑安排了介绍时间表的「主稿配发短文」，有关政策的讨论则留在主稿。

words.enDefinition: Fixing a factual error in published news without notifying readers that the correction was made.

examples.en: The reviewer called it a silent correction because the outlet fixed a timetable error without acknowledging the change.
examples.zh: 媒体改正了时间表里的错误，却没有说明这一改动，审校人员称其为「未说明的新闻更正」。

examples.en: Our class discussed why a silent correction could confuse readers who had already shared the earlier article.
examples.zh: 全班讨论了「未说明的新闻更正」为何可能让已经分享旧版文章的读者困惑。

words.enDefinition: A controlled setting that mimics selected features of a market to study potential buying behavior.

examples.en: The simulated test market showed students several fictional packages before recording which product they would select.
examples.zh: 「模拟试销市场」先向学生展示几个虚构包装，再记录他们会选哪种产品。

examples.en: We compared the simulated test market with sales data from a limited release in local shops.
examples.zh: 我们把「模拟试销市场」与本地商店限量上架得到的销售数据作比较。

collocations: data from a simulated test market
set up a simulated test market

words.enDefinition: Simultaneous transmission of the same programme on different channels or platforms

examples.en: The mock schedule lists a simulcast on television and the broadcaster's website.
examples.zh: 模拟排期列出电视和播出机构网站的「同步播出」。

examples.en: We distinguished a simulcast from a stream made available after the broadcast.
examples.zh: 我们区分了「同步播出」与电视播出后才提供的网络播放。

words.enDefinition: the one central benefit or idea that a creative brief asks an advertisement to communicate

examples.en: The team chose a single-minded proposition about easier storage for the folding desk campaign.
examples.zh: 在折叠桌的广告中，团队选定的「单一核心主张」是更易收纳。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether the storyboard still expressed the single-minded proposition from the brief.
examples.zh: 导师问，分镜是否仍体现简报里的「单一核心主张」。

words.enDefinition: an advertisement that viewers can dismiss before the end, sometimes after a minimum viewing time

examples.en: The skippable ad displayed its main message early because viewers could leave after several seconds.
examples.zh: 观众几秒后可以离开，因此「可跳过广告」很早就显示了主信息。

examples.en: Our class compared how much of a skippable ad viewers watched across two versions.
examples.zh: 课堂比较了两个版本的「可跳过广告」分别被观众看完了多少。

words.enDefinition: The perceived possibility that a buying choice may be judged negatively by people important to the consumer.

examples.en: The fictional student worries teammates will disapprove of the new supplies, illustrating social risk of a purchase.
examples.zh: 虚构学生担心队友不认可新买的用品，体现了「购买的社会风险」。

examples.en: Our casebook asks whether concern about teammates' opinions reflects social risk of a purchase in the story.
examples.zh: 案例教材询问，故事中对队友看法的担心是否反映了「购买的社会风险」。

collocations: assess the social risk of a purchase
perceived social risk of a purchase
concern about the social risk of a purchase

words.enDefinition: Reporting centered on lifestyle, personal experience, or human interest rather than urgent public developments.

examples.en: The editor grouped the piece about students' favorite reading corners with the magazine's other soft news.
examples.zh: 编辑把介绍学生最喜欢的阅读角的文章归入杂志的其他「软新闻」。

examples.en: We compared soft news in the weekend section with the urgent transport reports on the front page.
examples.zh: 我们把周末版的「软新闻」与头版的紧急交通报道作比较。

words.enDefinition: A brief excerpt of recorded speech selected for a news report.

examples.en: The radio report included a sound bite in which the librarian explained the new opening hours.
examples.zh: 电台报道采用了一段「新闻采访短引语」，图书管理员在里面解释了新的开放时间。

examples.en: We listened to the full answer before choosing a sound bite for the student news bulletin.
examples.zh: 我们先听完整回答，再为学生新闻简报挑选一段「新闻采访短引语」。

collocations: include a sound bite in a report

words.enDefinition: Explaining relevant information about a source so readers can judge how it supports the story.

examples.en: The article's source disclosure explained that one quoted person helped organize the event under discussion.
examples.zh: 报道中的「消息来源说明」说明，被引用的一个人参与了文中活动的组织工作。

examples.en: We read the source disclosure to see which details about the speaker's role were public.
examples.zh: 我们阅读了「消息来源说明」，查看发言者哪些与报道相关的背景信息已经公开。

words.enDefinition: Assessing a source's credibility, access to information, and relevant interests before using their account.

examples.en: The editor required source vetting before relying on a contributor who claimed to know the timetable.
examples.zh: 一名投稿人称自己知道时间表，编辑要求先做「消息来源审查」，再决定是否采用。

examples.en: Our exercise separated source vetting from checking the dates that the fictional source had provided.
examples.zh: 练习把「消息来源审查」与核对虚构消息提供者给出的日期分开。

words.enDefinition: An offering for which buyers will make an unusual effort to obtain a preferred option.

examples.en: The class called it a specialty product because fictional buyers traveled specifically for that model.
examples.zh: 全班将它称作「特殊品」，因为虚构买家专程前去购买这一型号。

examples.en: We compared a specialty product with a similar item buyers would happily replace with another brand.
examples.zh: 我们把「特殊品」与一种相似商品作比较，后者的买家愿意换成其他品牌。

collocations: classify an item as a specialty product

words.enDefinition: Retail outlet concentrating on a limited category with relatively deep assortment

examples.en: The reading describes a specialty store with a large selection of bicycle accessories.
examples.zh: 阅读材料描述了一家自行车配件选择很多的「专业商店」。

examples.en: We compared the specialty store with a larger retailer carrying many unrelated categories.
examples.zh: 我们将这家「专业商店」与经营多个无关类别的大型零售商作了比较。

words.enDefinition: To decide that a prepared or proposed news story will not be published.

examples.en: The editor chose to spike a story when its central claim could not be verified for the issue.
examples.zh: 那期刊物截稿前没能核实稿件的核心说法，编辑决定「撤下待发报道」。

examples.en: Our classroom exercise asked what would justify a decision to spike a story after extensive reporting.
examples.zh: 课堂练习问，做了大量采访工作后，什么理由足以让编辑决定「撤下待发报道」。

collocations: a decision to spike a story

words.enDefinition: An information session or document preparing a spokesperson with relevant, verified facts and context before speaking.

examples.en: The fictional spokesperson briefing lists the revised dates and the department responsible for each part of the project.
examples.zh: 虚构「发言人情况简报」列出了调整后的日期，以及项目各环节的负责部门。

examples.en: Our case asks which facts should appear in the spokesperson briefing before the fictional media session begins.
examples.zh: 案例询问，虚构媒体活动开始以前应在「发言人情况简报」中列明哪些事实。

words.enDefinition: content whose production or distribution is funded by an outside sponsor

examples.en: The magazine marked the sponsored content above the article and identified the organization that funded it.
examples.zh: 杂志在文章上方标注「赞助内容」，并注明出资机构。

examples.en: The audience study asked whether readers understood who had paid for the sponsored content.
examples.zh: 受众研究询问读者是否知道谁为这篇「赞助内容」付费。

words.enDefinition: A statement making visible the fact that an organisation or activity receives support from an identified sponsor.

examples.en: The fictional exhibition's sponsorship disclosure names the organisation that contributed funding for the printed programme.
examples.zh: 虚构展览的「赞助关系披露」写明为印制日程册提供资金的机构。

examples.en: Our class asks whether the sponsorship disclosure is easy to locate in the fictional museum's public announcement.
examples.zh: 全班询问，在虚构博物馆的公开公告中是否能轻松找到「赞助关系披露」。

words.enDefinition: Meeting to identify where music or sound should enter or change

examples.en: The composer joins the spotting session to discuss where the music should begin.
examples.zh: 作曲人参加「声音点位讨论会」，商量音乐应该从哪里开始。

examples.en: We noted two silent moments during the spotting session for the short film.
examples.zh: 我们在短片的「声音点位讨论会」上记录了两处静默时刻。

words.enDefinition: A reporter employed as part of a publication's regular staff.

examples.en: The staff reporter took over the follow-up when the freelance contributor finished the first article.
examples.zh: 自由撰稿人完成首篇文章后，「媒体在职记者」接手了后续报道。

examples.en: The student newsroom listed its staff reporter beside the editor on the contact page for readers.
examples.zh: 学生新闻室在面向读者的联系页面上，把「媒体在职记者」列在编辑旁边。

collocations: a story by a staff reporter

words.enDefinition: Communication with groups or people who affect or are affected by an organisation's activities or decisions.

examples.en: The sample plan covers stakeholder communications with staff, local residents, and groups that use the fictional venue.
examples.zh: 样本计划涵盖与虚构场地的工作人员、当地居民及使用团体的「利益相关方沟通」。

examples.en: Our class discusses stakeholder communications when reviewing who needs information about the fictional library's shortened hours.
examples.zh: 全班回顾哪些人需要了解虚构图书馆缩短开放时间的信息，并讨论「利益相关方沟通」。

words.enDefinition: A process of involving affected or interested groups through activities such as consultation, dialogue, or partnership.

examples.en: The fictional college includes stakeholder engagement so library users can comment on options for the temporary space.
examples.zh: 虚构大学安排「利益相关方参与」，让图书馆使用者可以就临时场地的选项发表意见。

examples.en: Our casebook distinguishes stakeholder engagement from announcements that only tell people which option was selected in the example.
examples.zh: 案例教材把「利益相关方参与」与示例中只告知选定哪一方案的公告区分开。

words.enDefinition: The confidence that affected or interested groups have in an organisation's reliability, honesty, or conduct.

examples.en: The fictional evaluation measures stakeholder trust after the museum publishes several timely corrections to its notices.
examples.zh: 博物馆及时更正几则通知后，虚构评估衡量了「利益相关方信任」。

examples.en: The report treats stakeholder trust as an intermediate outcome before examining longer-term changes in community participation.
examples.zh: 报告将「利益相关方信任」视为中期结果，然后考察社区参与较长期的变化。

words.enDefinition: A brand with a distinct public identity and little visible connection to its owner or sister brands.

examples.en: The fictional company sold lamps under a standalone brand with no parent name on the box.
examples.zh: 虚构公司以「独立品牌」销售台灯，包装盒上没有母公司名称。

examples.en: We asked whether the new line should share the main name or become a standalone brand.
examples.zh: 我们讨论新产品线应当沿用主名称，还是成为一个「独立品牌」。

collocations: market an offering as a standalone brand

words.enDefinition: An editor responsible for interpreting and applying a newsroom's editorial standards.

examples.en: The standards editor reviewed whether the draft explained its use of an unnamed source clearly enough.
examples.zh: 「新闻规范编辑」审查了草稿是否充分说明采用匿名消息来源的原因。

examples.en: We asked the standards editor how the fictional newsroom should describe the mistake in its notice.
examples.zh: 我们问「新闻规范编辑」，虚构新闻室应怎样在公告里说明这处错误。

collocations: a review by the standards editor

words.enDefinition: Proportion of defined observations or demand occasions when stock is unavailable

examples.en: The store comparison reports the stockout rate based on daily checks for selected products.
examples.zh: 商店对比以对指定商品的每日检查为依据，报告「缺货率」。

examples.en: We discussed why the stockout rate changed when the observation window became longer.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了为什么观察时段延长时，「缺货率」会发生变化。

words.enDefinition: Branded retail space operating within a larger host retailer's premises

examples.en: The fictional bookstore hosts a store-within-a-store selling supplies for art students.
examples.zh: 虚构书店引入了一个向艺术专业学生销售用品的「店中店」。

examples.en: We marked the store-within-a-store separately from the host's own merchandise on the plan.
examples.zh: 我们在平面图上将「店中店」与主商店自己的商品分开标注。

words.enDefinition: A particular piece of coverage assigned to a reporter or reporting team.

examples.en: Her first story assignment was to interview the organizers and verify the schedule for the campus festival.
examples.zh: 她的首个「报道任务」是采访组织人员，并核实校园节日活动的日程。

examples.en: The editor shared the story assignment with two students who could attend different parts of the meeting.
examples.zh: 编辑把「报道任务」分给两名学生，两人可以分别旁听会议的不同环节。

collocations: give a reporter a story assignment

words.enDefinition: A newsroom planning list of proposed or scheduled coverage for a publication period.

examples.en: The story budget listed each planned article with its deadline and expected length for the next issue.
examples.zh: 「报道计划清单」列出下一期准备刊登的每篇报道及其截稿时间和预计篇幅。

examples.en: We checked the story budget before promising a second article about the same campus event.
examples.zh: 我们先看了「报道计划清单」，再答应就同一校园活动再写一篇报道。

collocations: add an item to the story budget

words.enDefinition: A coordinated set of related news pieces or materials published together.

examples.en: The newsroom assembled a story package with a main article, a timeline, and a short explainer.
examples.zh: 新闻室组建了「成套报道」，包括主稿、时间线和一篇简短的解释性报道。

examples.en: Our student team built a story package around the new bus route instead of relying on one article.
examples.zh: 学生小组围绕公交新线路组织了「成套报道」，用多篇内容来呈现。

collocations: a story package on a local issue

words.enDefinition: A reporter's proposal to an editor explaining an idea, its significance, and how to report it.

examples.en: The student editor accepted the story pitch because it identified a timely question and possible sources.
examples.zh: 学生编辑接受了这份「新闻选题提案」，因为它找准了一个当前值得报道的问题，并列出可能的消息来源。

examples.en: We revised the story pitch after realizing the original idea was too broad for one article.
examples.zh: 我们意识到原来的构想太宽，一篇报道写不下，就修改了「新闻选题提案」。

words.enDefinition: A short identifier used to label a story in an editorial workflow.

examples.en: The story slug identified the library article while editors were still deciding on its public headline.
examples.zh: 编辑还在商量对外刊登的标题时，用「稿件内部简称」标识这篇图书馆报道。

examples.en: We kept the same story slug when the headline changed because the assignment itself stayed the same.
examples.zh: 由于报道任务本身没变，修改标题时我们沿用了原来的「稿件内部简称」。

words.enDefinition: A fact-focused account of an event that keeps interpretation and personal opinion separate.

examples.en: The campus paper published a straight news report summarizing the library board's decision and its starting date.
examples.zh: 校园报发表了一篇「直述新闻报道」，概述图书馆委员会的决定及生效日期。

examples.en: Our class turned the student writer's notes into a straight news report rather than an opinion column.
examples.zh: 全班把学生作者的笔记写成「直述新闻报道」，没有写成评论专栏。

collocations: the lead of a straight news report

words.enDefinition: A freelance contributor who supplies coverage to an outlet as needed, often from a particular locality.

examples.en: The regional desk asked its local stringer to cover a meeting the staff could not attend.
examples.zh: 地区新闻组请当地「特约供稿记者」去报道一场本部记者无法参加的会议。

examples.en: The student publication credited a stringer who regularly sent short reports from the second campus.
examples.zh: 学生刊物在报道上注明一名「特约供稿记者」的姓名，此人经常从第二校区发来简讯。

words.enDefinition: Schedule board using movable strips to organize scenes and shooting days

examples.en: The stripboard makes it easy to group scenes that share a location.
examples.zh: 「场次条形排期表」方便将使用同一拍摄地点的场次排在一起。

examples.en: We rearranged the stripboard when two performers became unavailable that afternoon.
examples.zh: 两位演员当天午后无法出席，我们便调整了「场次条形排期表」。

words.enDefinition: Scheduling the same programme at a consistent time on multiple consecutive days

examples.en: The channel uses stripped scheduling for the same series across the weekday timetable.
examples.zh: 这个频道在工作日时间表中为同一剧集采用「固定日播排期」。

examples.en: We distinguished stripped scheduling from a programme appearing only once each week.
examples.zh: 我们把「固定日播排期」与每周只播一次的节目安排区分开来。

words.enDefinition: A distinct identity linked closely to a master brand and modifying its meaning for particular offerings.

examples.en: The fictional master brand added a study sub-brand while keeping its main name prominent on the packaging.
examples.zh: 虚构主品牌增设了一个学习用品「子品牌」，包装仍突出主品牌名称。

examples.en: Our chart showed how the sub-brand appealed to students while still clearly belonging to the master brand.
examples.zh: 我们的图说明「子品牌」如何吸引学生，同时仍明确隶属于主品牌。

collocations: connect a sub-brand with its master brand

words.enDefinition: a secondary headline that clarifies or develops the main headline in an advertisement

examples.en: The subheadline specified which three weekday evenings were available for the free evening sessions.
examples.zh: 「广告副标题」列明哪三个工作日晚上有免费的晚间课程。

examples.en: The art director gave the subheadline a smaller type size than the text above it.
examples.zh: 美术指导把「广告副标题」的字号设得比上方文字小。

words.enDefinition: Loss of subscribers through cancellations or nonrenewals over a defined period

examples.en: The mock service reports subscriber churn separately from a decline in viewing minutes.
examples.zh: 模拟服务把「订阅用户流失」与观看分钟数减少分开报告。

examples.en: We compared subscriber churn before and after two fictional membership periods ended.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两个虚构订阅周期结束前后的「订阅用户流失」情况。

words.enDefinition: On-demand access to a video catalogue through a paid subscription

examples.en: The case gives members unlimited access to a catalogue through subscription video on demand.
examples.zh: 案例通过「订阅式视频点播」向会员提供可不限次数观看的片库。

examples.en: We compared subscription video on demand with paying separately to rent a single title.
examples.zh: 我们将「订阅式视频点播」与另付费租看单部作品作了比较。

collocations: subscriber to subscription video on demand

words.enDefinition: Setting the time when each subtitle begins and ends on screen

examples.en: The final edit is ready, so the team can start subtitle spotting now.
examples.zh: 最终剪辑已准备好，团队现在可以开始「字幕时间轴定位」。

examples.en: We reviewed subtitle spotting for lines spoken across a change of shot.
examples.zh: 我们检查了跨镜头切换时说出的台词的「字幕时间轴定位」。

words.enDefinition: A story opening stating the most important verified facts immediately.

examples.en: The summary lead gave the reopening date, location, and reason for the delay in one concise paragraph.
examples.zh: 「概述式导语」用简练的一段交代了重新开放日期、地点和延误原因。

examples.en: We used a summary lead because readers needed the confirmed timetable before any personal accounts.
examples.zh: 我们采用「概述式导语」，因为读者需要先看到核实后的时间表，再读个人讲述。

words.zhGloss: 多客户共享的标准化调研
words.enDefinition: Research designed and produced by a provider for multiple clients who receive access to common findings or data.
acceptedZhAnswers: 多客户共享的标准化调研

examples.en: The class reads a simulated syndicated research summary that several fictional clients can access for the same category.
examples.zh: 全班阅读一个「多客户共享的标准化调研」的模拟摘要，多个虚构客户可查阅该品类的这一摘要。

examples.en: Our class compares syndicated research and custom research when reviewing the two sample proposals for a study.
examples.zh: 全班审阅两份调研样本提案时，比较了「多客户共享的标准化调研」和定制调研。

words.enDefinition: a unit of cumulative advertising exposure measured against a defined target group only

examples.en: One target rating point corresponds to impressions equal to one percent of the selected audience.
examples.zh: 一个「目标受众收视点」对应的累计展示次数，相当于指定受众人数的百分之一。

examples.en: The report used a target rating point measure for the age group identified in the brief.
examples.zh: 报告对简报指定的年龄群体采用「目标受众收视点」指标。

words.enDefinition: Arrangement granting one partner sole distribution rights in a specified territory

examples.en: The fictional agreement grants territorial exclusivity to one distributor within the marked region.
examples.zh: 虚构协议赋予一家分销商在地图所标区域内的「区域独家经营」权。

examples.en: Our group drew the boundary to explain territorial exclusivity in the sample contract.
examples.zh: 我们组画出了区域边界，解释合同示例中的「区域独家经营」。

words.enDefinition: Distribution permissions limited to specified geographical markets under an agreement

examples.en: The classroom agreement grants territorial rights for one region but excludes neighboring markets.
examples.zh: 课堂协议授予一个地区的「地域发行权」，不包括邻近市场。

examples.en: We marked which territorial rights the fictional distributor would receive on the map.
examples.zh: 我们在地图上标出了虚构发行商会获得的「地域发行权」范围。

words.enDefinition: Licensing a screen title's distribution rights separately for distinct geographical markets

examples.en: The workbook breaks territory sales into separate agreements for three geographical markets.
examples.zh: 练习册将「分地区版权销售」拆为对应三个地理市场的不同协议。

examples.en: We checked how territory sales contributed to the classroom production's projected revenue.
examples.zh: 我们查看「分地区版权销售」如何为课堂制作项目带来预计收入。

words.enDefinition: one group or condition receiving a defined treatment in an advertising test

examples.en: Each test cell saw a different creative version while the rest of the exhibition page stayed fixed.
examples.zh: 每个「广告测试组」看到的广告创意版本不同，展览页面的其他内容固定。

examples.en: The researcher checked the sample size for each test cell before interpreting the change in signups.
examples.zh: 研究人员解读报名量变化前，先核对各「广告测试组」的样本量。

collocations: assign viewers to a test cell

words.enDefinition: Offering a product on a limited scale to observe how the market responds.

examples.en: The fictional shop used test marketing at one campus branch before considering a wider launch.
examples.zh: 虚构商店先在一个校区门店进行「试销」，再考虑更大范围上市。

examples.en: We checked whether test marketing measured actual purchases rather than only stated interest in the concept.
examples.zh: 我们核对「试销」是否衡量了实际购买，而不只是顾客口头表达的兴趣。

words.enDefinition: advertising that uses an individual's account or endorsement to support a product or organization

examples.en: The repair shop chose testimonial advertising and asked a customer to describe a recent visit.
examples.zh: 维修店选择「证言式广告」，请一位顾客讲述最近的一次到店经历。

examples.en: The class reviewed testimonial advertising featuring customers who had actually used the equipment shown.
examples.zh: 课程回顾了几则「证言式广告」，出镜顾客都实际用过所展示的设备。
